'Not again': Arrest of US marine for murder reignites protests in Japan's Okinawa
- Published
For many Okinawa locals, the arrest of a US soldier accused of robbing and killing a woman in a hotel room has reignited decades of frustration over crimes involving US military personnel there.
"Honestly my first reaction was, 'Not again,'" 52-year-old longtime Okinawa resident Ai Sato told the BBC.
"Nothing has changed since I was a child. How many times are we going to repeat the same thing, create more victims, cause their families to suffer, and ultimately, cause the people of Okinawa to grieve?"
Akemi Oshiro, a 62-year-old Ginowan resident shared similar sentiments.
"I know we shouldn't get used to terrible things like this, but because they keep happening, I've stopped being surprised," she told the BBC.
Okinawa hosts the largest US military presence in Japan. It is home to several US military bases and tens of thousands of American troops.
US Marine Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, was arrested by Japanese police on Sunday. Police say an investigation is underway and that Ballard is in Japanese custody because the alleged crime was unrelated to official military duties.
Whether a US service member is acting in the performance of official duty, external or not can determine which country has primary jurisdiction. When Japan has jurisdiction, but the suspect is under US custody, they can retain custody until Japan brings charges.
Ballard was assigned to III Marine Expeditionary Force and stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma in Ginowan City.
The Okinawa prefectural police say 39-year-old Anna Yagi was found dead early 3 October in a hotel room in Naha.
Security footage allegedly shows a man believed to be the suspect entering the hotel with the woman and leaving alone with her belongings. Local media citing police have reported that Yagi appeared to have been strangled with a cord.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi registered an official protest with Washington. But residents like Sato feel that's far from enough.
"I am deeply disappointed by the same kinds of government comments we have been hearing for decades -- that they will protest or that they take the matter seriously."
"I want Prime Minister Takaichi to call President Trump directly, someone with whom she has been emphasizing as having a close relationship with, and discuss concrete measures to prevent this from happening yet again," she said.
Following news of the suspected murder, people in Japan have been voicing anger with some 100 people protesting in both Naha and Tokyo. Others took to social media expressing their outrage and demanding justice with one user saying: "Enough is enough."
Over the past few years, a number of accidents and crimes have led to growing local opposition to the US presence on the island.
The 2016 rape and murder of a 20-year-old local woman saw tens of thousands of protesters demonstrate against the heavy US presence there. A former US marine subsequently received a life sentence for the crime.
The US currently has about 55,000 military personnel stationed in Japan, with the heaviest concentration based on the tropical island prefecture. Okinawa is one of the country's smallest prefectures by size, but 70% of the land used exclusively by the US military in Japan is located there.
In 1972, Okinawa prefecture was returned to Japanese control after United States forces occupied the islands at the end of the Second World War. Since then, there have been 6,409 arrests for criminal offenses related to US military personnel, according to Okinawa Prefectural Government.
Locals say the significant US presence has stirred resentment over a number of issues from crimes including rapes, assaults, and drunk-driving accidents to local disturbances such as noise and aircraft crashes.
In 1995, three US servicemen abducted, beat, and raped a 12-year-old schoolgirl as she walked home from a stationery store.
In 2025, a US Marine was convicted of choking and sexually assaulting a Japanese woman.
"Even 80 yeas after the war, Okinawa where we live is a place that is so unnerving," 48-year-old mother of two boys Hitomi Miyagi told the BBC.
"We will not stop raising our voices hoping for an Okinawa, where we can live in peace."

The organising president of the Alpine skiing World Championships in Crans-Montana in February was suspended on Wednesday as he awaits trial for fraud in his business.

“This decision follows the indictment of Claude-Alain Schmidhalter by the public prosecutor’s office of Valais canton,” Swiss Ski said in a statement, adding the criminal case is not related to the sport and he retains the presumption of innocence.

Crans-Montana hosts the Alpine worlds from February 1, just 13 months after a devastating fire at a bar in the resort popular with young people. It killed 41 people and injured 115. The bar owners and multiple public officials face charges arising from the incident.

150 days of Himanta govt in Assam: People's favourite but nature built a fury
It has been 150 days since the Himanta Biswa Sarma-led BJP government returned to power in Assam. From infrastructure and welfare, Himanta 'Mama' has a mass appeal, but the rare floods have sparked rare discontentment. Here's a 360-degree view.
Five months into his second term as Assam Chief Minister, Himanta Biswa Sarma remains the BJP's biggest political asset in the northeast. The mandate he secured in the 2026 Assembly election was not merely a victory for the BJP but a reaffirmation of Himanta's personal appeal, with the party winning 82 and the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) taking its tally to 102 in Assam's 126-member House.
Though Himanta's mass appeal remains largely intact, the first 150 days of the new government paint a complicated picture.
Himanta's government has pushed infrastructure, welfare and investment while his political persona has become increasingly personalised. Yet, for a government that has made development a central political pitch, nature's fury — particularly the devastating floods — created the biggest challenge.
Beyond floods, unemployment, price rise, indigenous rights and environmental concerns are emerging as pressure points. A fragmented opposition, meanwhile, has so far struggled to turn this discontent into a credible political challenge.
Therefore, for Himanta, the second term has begun with both an advantage and a warning. The people still see him as their "Mama" (maternal uncle), but expectations of the man who has been running a one-man show in Assam's politics for more than a decade are now considerably higher.
"The BJP in Assam has been struggling to meet people's expectations and is facing a big challenge to prevent growing discontent among the people over inflation, unemployment and poor disaster management," Guwahati-based senior journalist Sushanta Talukdar told India Today Digital.
Himanta Biswa Sarma is leading the third successive BJP government in Assam. The BJP first came to power in Assam in 2016 and the government was led by Sarbananda Sonowal. Himanta took over as the CM after the 2021 election and Sonowal was made a Union minister.
CM HIMANTA'S MAMA POLITICS IN ASSAM SHINES BRIGHT
Himanta Biswa Sarma's popularity is seen in his ability to turn the formal image of a chief minister into something more intimate.
The "Mama" tag began as a way children and people of Assam address him and has become a wider political identity. During the 2026 Assembly election campaign, the image was amplified through social media, beneficiary interactions and rallies. Himanta's dance to the BJP campaign song — Aaru ebar Modi Sarkar (Modi government one more time) — at rallies, an unusual sight for a chief minister but one that fitted the increasingly informal political persona he had cultivated in Assam.
The dance videos mattered because they reinforced the idea of a leader who was not distant from his audience. At one rally, supporters joined Sarma in dancing, with voters describing the atmosphere as one of "phurti" (merriment), and saying he felt like a member of their family.
The electoral result showed how effectively that image has travelled beyond the BJP's traditional support base. The party increased its tally from 60 seats in 2021 to 82 in 2026, while the NDA secured 102 seats.
But popularity also creates a higher level of accountability.
"The expectations from the Himanta government remain very high and issues such as employment, price rise and implementation on the ground continue to influence the public perception," Preety Priyadarshinee, an independent journalist who has been covering Assam for nearly 10 years, told India Today Digital.
"The issues of inflation and unemployment are frustrating the people of Assam," she added.
ASSAM FLOODS: THE BIGGEST TEST OF GOVERNANCE FOR HIMANTA ADMINISTRATION
If development and personal brand are Sarma's political strength, disaster management has emerged as one of his biggest challenges. During his first 150 days of the second term, the Assam CM's one-man show had only one opponent, and that was not from any politician but a natural disaster.
The 2026 floods, one of the worst in recent decades, hit Upper Assam particularly hard. By August 17, the official death toll from the floods reached 105, with Sivasagar recording the highest number of fatalities. Nearly 32,000 people were still affected across four districts at that point, while embankments, roads, bridges and agricultural land had also suffered damage, according to ANI.
The government mounted relief operations and announced assistance for affected families. Orunodoi beneficiaries in the four worst-affected districts were also given an additional Rs 2,500 as relief.
But the political criticism has been sharper than the relief measures.
"The biggest challenge it faced [was] in rescue, relief and rehabilitation work during catastrophic floods," Talukdar told India Today Digital, arguing that the crisis exposed weaknesses in the government's claims of administrative efficiency.
Priyadarshinee was more critical about the impact on affected communities, describing the floods as a disaster that pushed badly hit areas backwards and alleging that promised compensation had not reached many victims.
For CM Sarma, this is a particularly difficult problem because floods are not an occasional political issue in Assam. They are a recurring governance test. A government that wants to project Assam as an investment and infrastructure destination must also demonstrate that development can coexist with resilience against floods and erosion.
DEVELOPMENT HAS BECOME HIMANTA'S BIGGEST STRENGTH
The BJP government has used its first 150 days to establish continuity with Sarma's first term. Roads, bridges, welfare delivery, healthcare and investment remain central to its political pitch.
The 2026-27 Budget, presented in July, laid out an ambitious development programme, including a target of creating two lakh jobs over five years, large road and connectivity projects and a renewed investment push. In the previous term, he had promised a lakh jobs, and overshot his promise by giving employment to 1.6 lakh people.
Orunodoi remains one of the government's most visible welfare instruments. Under Orunodoi 3.0, more than 37 lakh women are receiving Rs 1,250 a month through direct benefit transfer (DBT).
The Tata Group's Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility, which is the flagship semiconductor investment associated with CM Himanta, has begun its pilot production operations, but is not fully operational. The CM on October 3 announced that the first clean room of the project was ready to produce chips. A second clean room is under construction and will be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in December 2026 or January 2027.
Priyadarshinee told India Today Digital that the government had made progress on infrastructure, welfare and administrative initiatives. She pointed to the expansion of connectivity, bridges such as Dhola-Sadiya and Bogibeel, and infrastructure projects in Guwahati.
"There were a lot of job opportunities that opened up," she said, while also noting the wider development push and peace accords with insurgent groups.
"The BJP government's major commitments — including two lakh jobs, higher welfare assistance and stronger flood control — would require more time to assess actual outcomes," said Purna Bikash Bora, India Today Group's Assam Correspondent.
That distinction is important. Because this is Himanta's second term as the chief minister of Assam. At this stage, Assam has seen a strong pipeline of promises and projects, but the real test is whether these produce jobs, higher incomes and better public services.
LACK OF JOBS AND PRICE RISE: THE EXPECTATION GAP IN ASSAM
The employment question is also important in that state because the government's own numbers show the scale of the challenge.
As of June 30, more than 15.43 lakh active jobseekers were registered with Assam's Directorate of Skill, Employment and Entrepreneurship, including more than 3.55 lakh fresh registrations in the first half of 2026.
That makes the Budget's promise of two lakh jobs over five years politically significant, but it also means the government will increasingly be judged by actual employment outcomes rather than announcements.
"The voters expected that prices of essential commodities would be reduced, and there would be more jobs. Discontent against the BJP-led government is brewing because of its failure to curb the price hike and create employment," senior journalist Talukdar told India Today Digital.
One has to understand that inflation isn't a state-specific issue. The conflict in the Middle East has disrupted energy supply routes and led to a price rise in commodities.
Political Analyst Abhinav Borbora points to the disquiet among the middle class and the youth.
"I see some kind of disquiet amongst a section of the middle class and the youth. It might be because of the way the government is responding, say, to a lot of criticism and the way it is responding, which is probably often not in a very tasteful way. It might also be because of allegations of corruption," Borbora told India Today Digital.
The Himanta-led BJP government has won a massive mandate, and these points are more of an early warning than an immediate electoral threat.
RIGHTS, EVICTIONS AND THE QUESTION OF POWER IN ASSAM
The Himanta government's aggressive administrative style has also generated questions about civil liberties and the treatment of protesters among a section of the population, the journalists said.
Eviction drives have been a flashpoint, with the government maintaining that it is clearing encroachments from public land, while opponents have alleged that the drives disproportionately affect Muslims.
The Mumtaz Begum case added a sharper legal dimension. Begum, declared a foreigner by a Foreigners' Tribunal, was pushed into Bangladesh in June. The Gauhati High Court later criticised the manner in which the process was handled and ordered the Assam government to pay Rs 2 lakh interim compensation to her husband while asking the Ministry of External Affairs to help trace and facilitate her return.
The case has become a reminder that Assam's citizenship and migration politics remain deeply sensitive, and that administrative efficiency cannot come at the expense of due process, said Priyadarshinee.
Cockroach Janta Party co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka's visit to the state and his brief detention drew criticism from the outfit, which alleged that the action was an attempt to intimidate voices of dissent.
AN OPPOSITION THAT HAS NOT FOUND ITS MOMENT UNDER HIMANTA'S DOMINANCE
One of the biggest advantages for Sarma is the weakness of the opposition. The Congress, the principal opposition party in recent years, managed to win just 19 seats in the 126-member Assembly.
Priyadarshinee said the opposition has a presence but remains fragmented.
"The main opposition now doesn't feel like the Congress because, in the recent elections that happened, the Vidhan Sabha elections, the Congress only won the minority seats in the state, which was a narrative already made by BJP," she said. "A lot of senior leaders of the Congress like Bhupen Borah and Pradyut Bordoloi joined the BJP at the last moment, indicating the infighting within the party," she said, arguing that a meaningful challenge would require the Congress, Akhil Gogoi's Raijor Dal and the Lurinjyoti Gogoi-led Assam Jatiya Parishad to build a common narrative.
That weakness has given Sarma considerable political room in the state. Even outside the Assembly, the trend has continued. In the October 3 Silchar Municipal Corporation election, the BJP-led NDA won 34 of 42 seats, with the BJP taking 32.
SO, WHAT'S THE 150-DAY VERDICT FOR THE HIMANTA GOVERNMENT?
Is Himanta Biswa Sarma's second-term government succeeding? The answer, at 150 days, moves closer to a yes but isn't overwhelmingly affirmative.
There is visible momentum in infrastructure, welfare, investment and administrative delivery. There is also little doubt that Sarma has built a personal political brand that goes beyond the BJP organisation. His persona, his campaign theatrics and his ability to connect with beneficiaries have helped turn him into Assam's defining political figure.
But the same personalisation raises the stakes.
As political analyst Borbora put it, with Sarma's government now entering another term, "there are signs of high-handedness" among sections of the political establishment. He warned that the government risks alienating people if it does not address that tendency.
The floods have exposed the limits of infrastructure-led governance. Job numbers show the scale of the unemployment challenge. Price concerns remain. Kaziranga has brought development into conflict with conservation. Tribal and indigenous questions remain unresolved. Citizenship cases continue to test due process. And sections of civil society remain uneasy about the use of state power.
The opposition has so far been too divided to capitalise on these grievances.
For now, therefore, Himanta remains Assam's "Mama" who is popular, powerful and politically dominant. But the next phase of his second term will be about proving that the development model that made him popular can withstand Assam's most difficult realities.

Pretorius breaks Gayle's T20 record score
- Published
CSA T20 Challenge, Bloemfontein
Titans 267-3 (20 overs): Pretorius 188* (79); Boast 1-46
Knights 143 (17.2 overs): Cloete 39 (25); Ferreira 3-16
Titans won by 124 runs
Lhuan-dre Pretorius has broken Chris Gayle's record for the highest score in a men's T20 match with an unbeaten 188 in a domestic fixture in South Africa.
The 20-year-old South African's knock off 79 deliveries, including 13 sixes and 15 fours, helped Titans post 267-3 against Knights in the CSA T20 Challenge.
It eclipsed the 175 made by Gayle for Royal Challengers Bangalore (now Bengaluru) against Pune Warriors in the 2013 Indian Premier League.
Pretorius, who has played 17 T20s, three one-dayers and two Tests for South Africa, finished with a strike rate of 237.97.
He made his half-century off 24 balls but only required 16 more balls to get to three figures and then got to 150 off just 58 deliveries.
Titans then bowled out Knights for 143 to wrap up an emphatic 124-run victory at the Mangaung Oval in Bloemfontein.

The most profitable move in artificial intelligence may no longer be selling intelligence. It is selling a model to a company, wiring it into that company's most valuable work, learning the business from the inside, and then shipping the product that competes with it. In a previous piece for Inc42, I argued that the black box was losing the boardroom, and that enterprise AI built on the customer's own terms was the opening worth chasing. The months since have made the argument more literal than expected. The frontier labs are now moving into their customers' markets, and they are doing it in plain sight. The Pattern Has Hardened Into A Playbook Read the moves of the past year together and a sequence emerges. Sell the model to the world's most valuable businesses. Help wire it into their most sensitive and highest-margin work. Map how the business runs from the inside. Then turn those learnings into a product and stand up as the customer's competitor. Each step, taken alone, reads as partnership. Assembled, they read as strategy. Of course, a lot still depends on execution. Just because a model company knows how a customer runs its business does not mean it can run that business better than the customer. However, the labs would say this is simply where the technology leads, and that is part of the truth. It is also the most dependable way to convert a supplier relationship into a market entrant position. Figma is the clearest illustration. It partnered with Anthropic on AI design tooling, the kind of collaboration that looks like validation for a newly public company. Then Mike Krieger, Anthropic's chief product officer, resigned from Figma's board, and three days later Anthropic launched Claude Design, a standalone tool aimed squarely at Figma. The stock fell around 7% on the day, and the activist fund Findell Capital has since pushed the board to review the entire Anthropic relationship. Asked about it at a closed event, Figma's Dylan Field reached for the exact phrase OpenAI's board once used to remove Sam Altman, saying the lab had not been "consistently candid." The partner had become the competitor inside a single news cycle. Harvey is a more practical example, because the evidence sits on Anthropic's own website, which still features the legal startup as a customer success story for contract analysis, due diligence and litigation. In May, Anthropic launched Claude for Legal and began selling those same workflows directly to law firms. Harvey carries an $11 Bn valuation, and the model that powered the challenger now stands beside it as a rival. The pattern repeats wherever a workflow is worth owning. Intercom built its support agents on OpenAI's models, and OpenAI now sells Presence, its own voice and chat support agent. Abridge and Ambience built clinical documentation on OpenAI's API, and OpenAI now sells ChatGPT for Healthcare to hospitals, with a free tier for individual clinicians and documentation built in. Benchling embedded Claude into biotech R&D across more than 1,300 companies, and Anthropic now sells its own research workbench, Claude Science. The same logic is reaching financial services, where Claude connects to market-data providers and runs credit memos and know-your-customer checks inside banks. In each case the supplier watched the customer prove the market, then walked into it. The strength of this incentive also shows up clearly in the earliest partnerships within the industry. Microsoft owns roughly 27% of OpenAI. It had bought GitHub in 2018 for $7.5 Bn. OpenAI is now building a jobs platform for professional hiring and, as per reporting in The Information, a code repository, moves that would sit against LinkedIn and GitHub, both Microsoft properties. This is not a claim that anyone has been denied. It is a measure of how far the pull toward the customer's market reaches, when it can tug even against an early strategic investor's own businesses. Pharma Is Where the Trap Is Sharpest Drug discovery is the case that should give every board pause. Novo Nordisk and Bristol Myers Squibb route revenue and workflow data into Claude, treating Anthropic as a supplier. In May, BMS placed Claude before more than 30,000 employees as what it called a shared intelligence platform across research, clinical development and manufacturing. On 30 June, Anthropic launched Claude Science and, in the same breath, announced it would run its own preclinical drug discovery programmes. The customers, through their unchecked reliance on the model, are funding what they treat as a vendor but is in fact a competitor lurking in the shadows, and are helping to sharpen the very capability that may one day contest their pipelines. The market read it at once. On the day, Schrödinger fell as much as 8.3%, Recursion 3.3% and IQVIA more than 2.3%. Anthropic frames the work around neglected diseases that large pharma overlooks, and that framing is fair as far as it goes. It does not change the structural fact that the vendor has walked onto the customer's field. The Economics Make Restraint Implausible Follow the money and the behaviour explains itself. Anthropic's revenue run rate reached about $65 Bn by the end of July, up from roughly $1 Bn in December 2024, at a $965 Bn valuation, with a filing already lodged for a listing that could come this autumn. OpenAI has roughly doubled to about $40 Bn in revenue. Eight of the Fortune 10 are already Claude customers, a sign of how much of the real economy now runs through a single supplier. Selling tokens is a commodity business with thin and contested margins. Selling the finished application into a market with real returns on capital is where the value pools. A company carrying a near-trillion-dollar valuation into public markets cannot credibly promise to leave the richest layer of the stack to its customers forever. None of this requires bad faith. The incentive is obvious, which is exactly what makes the move more likely. The AI Narrative Is Getting Harder To Reconcile This is where the public story and the operating record pull apart, and founders are reading one against the other. The labs speak the language of safety, abundance and responsible stewardship, and in the same year they have entered design, law, support, healthcare and drug discovery. The mood at the frontier can run further still. On the All-In podcast in August, investor Gavin Baker said he had been told by people he trusts that Dario Amodei has floated the idea that Anthropic "might be the only private company in the world" at some point, with only governments beside it. Anthropic rejected the account outright, with one of its researchers calling it false and Amodei rebutting it directly. Mark Zuckerberg has since published an essay making the opposite case, for open models and a distribution of power rather than its concentration. This episode matters not because it is settled, but because it is not. The claims are second-hand, disputed and changing week to week, and that instability is itself the point. Nobody, inside these companies or outside them, can tell you today how this resolves. Of course, this narrative is great support and justification for the enterprise value of an IPO this large. What is not in doubt is the direction of the incentive and the exposure it creates for everyone who builds on top. Alex Karp of Palantir has named the mechanism most plainly, arguing that enterprises are "paying for tokens that create no value" while surrendering their alpha, the proprietary edge that makes a business defensible. Michael Burry put it more bluntly, remarking that Anthropic was eating Palantir's lunch. The narratives will keep shifting. The opportunity arithmetic underneath them will not. Own Your Alpha For India the exposure is doubled. The country's software firms and its 1,900-plus global capability centres are among the heaviest consumers of frontier APIs, and its services industry wires client workflows through those same models, sending client alpha upstream with every integration. The lesson from the cases above is that being a large and loyal customer is no shield. It may simply be the reconnaissance. The opening is the same size as the risk, and it is the one I argued for last time, only more urgent now. Vertical AI built on domain depth the labs cannot see from the outside. Private and on-premise deployment of open models. Harnesses that keep proprietary data inside the building. Open-weight models isolated from the internet and run for a single enterprise. Intercom has already moved its agent partly onto its own in-house open-weights model rather than depend on a supplier that competes with it, and that is the direction of travel. India's sovereign-model efforts and its vertical software builders should read this moment as the start of a new market preference forming. Every Indian founder and CTO now faces the same reckoning before the next integration. It is to know precisely what alpha they are sending upstream, and whether they can protect it before it returns as somebody else's product. The labs may or may not become the last companies standing. The firms that decide early to own their alpha will not have to find out.

Lunch meet, then a Jantar Mantar protest bid: INDIA bloc MPs' bus trip brings Janpath to a halt
The three buses were stopped at the intersection of Janpath and Ashoka Road as the Delhi Police scrambled to prevent the MPs from reaching Jantar Mantar
INDIA bloc lawmakers, packed into three buses, attempted to launch another massive protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar but were stopped by the Delhi Police on Janpath, bringing a large part of New Delhi to a halt on a busy Wednesday.
The lawmakers were invited by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for a vegetarian lunch at a popular restaurant on Janpath. After the lunch was over, it was decided to proceed to Jantar Mantar to restart the protest, which began with Tuesday's march from Parliament to Akashvani Bhavan.
Rahul Gandhi detained on way to Jantar Mantar; Priyanka refuses to budge | Track LIVE updates
Deep Dive
While many parties joined the lunch hosted by Mallikarjun Kharge, the Samajwadi Party, which has 37 MPs in the Lok Sabha, skipped it, blaming a lack of communication from the Congress.
The three buses were stopped at the intersection of Janpath and Ashoka Road as the Delhi Police scrambled to prevent the MPs from reaching Jantar Mantar, a site frequently used by parties and groups to stage protests.
*Shri Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress President & Leader of Opposition (LoP), Rajya Sabha, addressed the media in New Delhi today.*
Addressing the media, Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge said, "All of us in the INDIA alliance will stage a protest at Jantar Mantar today; all key leaders will be present together. We will continue to protest in this manner until our demands are met."
Also Read | Akhilesh Yadav's SP skips Kharge's Delhi lunch, senior official blames 'delayed communication'
"Secondly, the Election Commission is repeatedly making mistakes at the behest of Modi ji. When Modi ji orchestrates such errors, it implies an attempt to destroy democracy in this country; he pays no heed to the Constitution. Therefore, we decided that it is our duty to convey the people's concerns to the entire nation. That is why Rahul ji is fighting, and all parties have united to inform the people across the country that their entitlements and rights are being taken away; we are striving to safeguard those rights. No matter how many cases are filed against us or how much intimidation is attempted, we will not be cowed; we will keep smiling and moving forward."
Rahul Gandhi told the media, "As I mentioned, approximately 300 MPs—from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha—wanted to meet the Election Commissioners yesterday; they wished to meet the three Election Commissioners, but they did not meet us. The Delhi Police stopped us, and yesterday they stated that we could not protest there.
"So today, we intend to go to the designated protest site—Jantar Mantar—and sit there once again to convey to the nation that, for us, Shri Gyanesh Kumar is not a legitimate Election Commissioner of the country. Modi ji, Amit Shah ji, Mohan Bhagwat, and Gyanesh Kumar ji have destroyed the country's democracy. And as I said yesterday—those who have done this are traitors, and we will take action against them. I am telling you right now: Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," he said.
When asked about the FIR against him and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul said, "I already have 45 FIRs; my goal is to reach 100. I want 100 FIRs to be registered against me; for me, every FIR is a medal."
For more than three hours, the buses were not allowed to proceed, and the busy intersection was barricaded, bringing traffic to a halt on Ashoka Road, Raisina Road and Janpath.
At 6 pm, the police started detaining some protesters and taking them away. Two buses carrying the MPs were also removed.
On Wednesday, nearly 300 Opposition MPs marched from Parliament to Akashvani Bhavan to step up pressure on Gyanesh Kumar and force him to resign.
The march, part of a series of events planned by the INDIA bloc against Kumar, was stopped by the Delhi Police near Akashvani Bhavan, less than 300 metres from Nirvachan Sadan, the poll body's central office. While most of the MPs and party supporters were detained and taken away, Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with Congress general secretary KC Venugopal and a few other party leaders, managed to enter the Akashvani Bhavan campus to continue their protest.

Vithya Ramraj is still unable to understand the hype and hoopla surrounding her.
The 28-year-old, who emerged as one of India’s standout performers at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, returned with three medals and a National record in the 400m hurdles, breaking P. T. Usha’s 42-year-old mark.
“In the last Asian Games (2023) in Hangzhou, I won three medals. I don’t know why I became popular this time,” she told a select gathering at a function organised by the Anna Nagar outlet of jewellery makers Tanishq on Wednesday.
She might sound modest, but her performance speaks for itself. She played the anchor role brilliantly to help India win the gold medal in the women’s 4x400m relay, ran a brilliant race to break Usha’s long-standing record in the 400m hurdles and did well to guide India to a silver in the 4x400m mixed relay.
Though Vithya is happy to have won bronze in the 400m hurdles at the Games with a record time of 54.75s, she and her personal coach, Nehpal Singh, felt she should focus on running sub-54 in the forthcoming season.
“My coach is not happy with my timing in the 400m hurdles at the Games in Japan. In India, I am not pushed enough. Hence, I am not able to go sub-54. I will work harder and try to achieve the timing my coach has demanded of me,” said Vithya.
READ: Smiles, tears and a searching gaze: Enduring images from India’s Nagoya Asian Games campaign
When asked about the facilities at the cruise ship where the team stayed at the Asian Games, Vithya replied that she had faced worse things. “I’ve lived in a room with 20 members. We lived like that for six years. There were no reservations during travel for competitions. My coach [Nehpal Singh] said, ‘Don’t care about anything. Just go and run the race.’”
In all probability, Vithya will make her debut at the World Athletics Championships next year in Beijing, and she hopes to do well. “I want Vithya to make it to the final. That’s the target,” said Nehpal.
According to Vithya, the key to her doing well at the Asian Games was the good sleep she had in Spala (Poland), where she trained prior to the Games. “I slept for 10 hours in these three months. That was what brought my performance,” she said.
She will be keen to maintain the sleep cycle prior to the Worlds, where she hopes to perform well.
At the end of the function, Vithya was given an eight-gram gold coin, while her coach, Nehpal, was given a cheque of ₹1 lakh by Tanishq.

Kavita Gupta’s U.S.-based Cineroost has boarded Prateek Vats’ second feature, “Chronicles of a Confession,” as producer, joining Payal Kapadia and Anurag Kashyap on the project, which starts shooting in early November.
Cineroost stepped in to handle global representation and U.S. markets, and to help get the film into production. It is the company’s next feature after Vir Das’ “Baara Number.”
Penned by Vidur Nauriyal, Vats and Shubham, the drama centers on a Kashmiri shawl seller who admits to a crime he didn’t commit, kicking off a series of events nobody saw coming. The script was chosen for the Busan International Film Festival‘s Asian Cinema Fund, under its script development strand.
Vats broke through with “Eeb Allay Ooo!,” which world premiered at the Pingyao Film Festival in 2019 and took the Golden Gateway award at the Mumbai Film Festival that year. The film went on to screen at the Berlinale in 2020 and at Tribeca’s first online edition.
Popular on Variety
Ranjan Singh of Flip Films (“Songs of Forgotten Trees,” “Vagachipaani”) produces alongside Dubai’s Action Filmz, India’s Etched Films and Khan & Kumar Productions (“Lovers in the Blue Night”). The project’s producing and creative base stretches across India, the U.S. and the U.A.E. Kashyap and Kapadia serve as executive producers.
Kashyap, who was involved in Vats’ first film, said the director had spent a long time on a script he envies. “I almost want to steal it. And since I can’t, I have jumped on board as an executive producer,” Kashyap said. “It is an honor to associate with someone as great as Payal Kapadia who I have seen sticking to her voice and her ground as a filmmaker and then there is my own producer Ranjan Singh. What was there in this to not want to be part of it.”
Anand Bansal (“Dhuin,” “Gamak Ghar,” “The Elephant Whisperers”) is behind the camera, with Rajesh Thanickan (“Santosh,” “Homebound”) as supervising producer. Devika Dave (“Boong,” “Sherni”) handles production design, Himani Dehalvi (“Trial by Fire”) costumes and Bigyna Dahal (“The Fable,” “Khauff”) sound design.
“Prateek’s films mix humor and political commentary in a unique way which I have always admired. And this new project takes this to an even higher level,” Kapadia said.
“‘Chronicles of a Confession’ has been brewing for some years and I am thrilled that it is going on floor now,” Vats said. “The film solidifies my collaboration with producer Ranjan Singh, who has been with me since my debut feature, ‘Eeb Allay Ooo!'”
Gupta’s earliest film projects, 13 years ago, were with Kashyap, and the two have remained close. “Strong writing, the best creators and a stellar global creative team, everything about this film aligned with my vision for Cineroost – rare, global and rooted,” Gupta said.
The film marks the second major step in building out Cineroost’s slate.
“Business from films is not for my sustenance but really for my soul and passion,” Gupta said. “I find that to be a strength in the work I do in the creative world. I have the privilege of flirting with risk more than others.”
	“A lot of my work for South Asian talent and projects has been under the radar,” she added. “I felt time has come for me to take bigger steps and come out from being in the shadows to do what I love, nurturing creative voices, enabling stories that matter and building bridges between divergent worlds.”

The ‘Abe Memorial Corridor,’ dedicated to the memories of India-Japan friendship and cultural ties, was inaugurated at the Rudraksh Convention Center in Varanasi on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) by Akie Abe, wife of former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.
“The Abe Memorial Corridor is a living classroom for new generation. Every young person who comes here will be able to learn how a far-sighted leader can give a new direction to the future of two countries,” said Mr. Adityanath, while inaugurating the corridor.
Mr. Adityanath added, “The true tribute to late Shinzo Abe San would be that the friendship between India and Japan grows stronger every year than it was the previous year. This corridor is not merely a place preserving the memories of former Prime Minister of Japan, late Shinzo Abe San, but also a living symbol of the unbreakable friendship, trust and shared heritage between India and Japan.”
“Rudraksh is a symbol of friendship between India and Japan. Japan gifted Rudraksh to Kashi and today Kashi is preserving forever in this very Rudraksh the memory of former PM of Japan, late Shinzo Abe San, a symbol of friendship with Japan. Today is a very important day for all of us. As we take this friendship to a new dimension, October 7 is also the day when, exactly 25 years ago, on this very day in 2001, Prime Minister Modi ji took oath for the first time as Chief Minister of Gujarat. The foundation of friendship between our Prime Minister and former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe was also laid during that period. In 2007, Modi ji visited Japan as CM of Gujarat. It was there that he met Shinzo Abe San for the first time. This friendship was not built on position, it was built on trust. Positions changed, but the friendship did not. The inauguration of a memorial corridor dedicated to the memory of that friendship on the day when 25 years of this journey of public service are being completed, there could not be a more beautiful coincidence,” said Mr. Adityanath.
Mr. Adityanath recalled Shinzo Abe’s visit to India for the first time as Prime Minister in 2007, and his push for strong India-Japan partnership. “In August 2007, when Shinzo Abe San visited India for the first time as Prime Minister, he addressed the Parliament of India and said that a strong India is in Japan’s best interest and a strong Japan is in India’s best interest. In 2014, Kashi-Kyoto Partner City Agreement was signed in Kyoto. In 2015, he witnessed Indian faith at Kashi’s Ganga Aarti. In 2017, he laid the foundation stone of the bullet train in Ahmedabad and took India into a new era of mobility. In 2018, Shinzo Abe San invited Prime Minister Modi ji to his private residence in Yamanashi, giving a personal touch to the relations between the two countries,” said the U.P. CM.

Tigray capital 'out of cash' as fighting escalates, resident tells BBC
A resident of Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia's Tigray region, says that the atmosphere is calm but people are very stressed after fighting broke out between government troops and the party that controls the region on Wednesday, raising fears of a return to full-scale civil war.
He says that many banks have been running low on cash for months, leaving people to rely on mobile banking, with fears that could now be blocked.

The State informed the Kerala High Court that in-principle approval had not been granted to Keralam for establishing an All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS).
The Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V.M. Syam Kumar enquired into the reason why Keralam was not prioritised for building an AIIMS, even though the matter had been pending for almost 10 years. The Bench was considering a petition seeking establishment of an AIIMS under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY).
The court observed that the matter was presently at the stage of inter-ministerial consultation and any decision for setting up an AIIMS could be taken only after the continuation of the PMSSY scheme for the next five financial years, FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31, was approved.
In a previous order, the court noted that the idea of having an AIIMS in Keralam was raised in June 2016 and four locations were identified for this purpose. The court opined that Keralam should be considered on a priority basis considering the density of population, and asked the Union government to take a conscious decision concerning the proposal for the institute.
Prioritising other States
The Deputy Solicitor General of India, O.M. Shalina, informed the court that since Keralam had better health-care conditions than other States, the Union government was prioritising those States with a weaker health sector. At this point the court enquired whether the Union government’s stand was that Keralam did not require an AIIMS. The court orally asked whether the hospitals in the State were a disqualification or a ‘handicap’ to consider the establishment of the institute. The court orally remarked that Keralam had the highest density of population in the country, and that the existing hospitals would not be sufficient to provide medical facilities to the needy and poor.
The Union government responded that while considering all other States and Union Territories, Keralam’s status was much better, and that was the reason for the delay in approval. The court then enquired why there was an AIIMS in Delhi and two or three institutes in some other States, if the criteria was availability of medical facilities.

Two-time world champion Luke Littler can still qualify for the Players Championship Finals in Minehead – but what else can he win?
His unprecedented 12-month clean sweep may be over following a crushing 10-4 defeat by Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam and a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix, but he can still qualify for next month's Players Championship Finals.
The world No 1 had won the first six premier events of the season following his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January with the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

He had been hoping to add the World Series of Darts Finals, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals trophies to complete a historic clean sweep of the year. But his bid was derailed by Clayton, who reeled off seven of the final eight legs to defeat the teenager before overcoming Luke Woodhouse in Leicester, where he suffered a 2-1 defeat in the double-in, double-out tournament.

Had he gone on to win the title, Littler would have become the first player to hold both the World Championship and World Youth titles.

The top 64 players on the ProTour Order of Merit qualify for the Minehead showpiece, with the projected cut-off expected to exceed £30,000 after all 34 events. Littler currently sits in 126th place with £10,500, while Mike De Decker occupies the final qualifying spot in 64th with £29,250.
That leaves 'The Nuke' with a slim route into Minehead, but he would likely need to reach the final of at least one - and potentially both - of the final two ProTour events to force his way into the field.
Littler won the 2025 title, defeating Nathan Aspinall 11-8 in the final.

"I'm glad he went to the World Youth Championship, but I think if he had got to the final, then maybe we would have seen him at the ProTours. There's no point going all the way down to Minehead if you're not going to play the Players Championship Finals as well.

In late September, two images circulated online purportedly showing ancient Egyptian sculptures depicting cats walking and resting on their owners.
One of the images shows a sculpture, possibly a wood carving, of a cat in a museum display as either standing or walking on a person at rest. The other image features a cat sitting right up against the chin of a person whose eyes appear to be open.
For example, on Sept. 29, a Facebook user posted a graphic (archived) featuring the two images, with text reading, "4,000-year-old statues prove cats have always ignored personal space." The post's caption adds, "Cats Have Been Sitting on Their Humans for 4,000 Years." The pair of images also spread on Threads and X (archived, archived).
(Nathanistic via Facebook)
Reverse image searches uncovered examples of the standing cat image on Facebook, Instagram and Threads, as well as the resting cat image on Instagram, Threads and X.
Cats prominently feature in ancient Egyptian artifacts, including in mummification. That may be one reason why some commenters under posts have posted remarks indicating they believe the images are authentic. Others mention artificial intelligence, saying they are skeptical about whether the images show actual artifacts that truly exist.
In sum, the images are fake and appear to be AI-generated — as do other images of Egyptian sculptures depicting cats interacting with people.
The aforementioned reverse image searches indicate that the earliest posts featuring the image of the cat standing or walking on top of the person first appeared on Soft Cat Memes (@softcatmemes) accounts on Facebook, Instagram and Threads on Sept. 25, as well as on the possibly-affiliated @hardcatmemes X account. The image contains overlaid text, reading, "Cats have been bothering their humans since the dawn of time."
(@softcatmemes via Facebook)
The image of the cat sitting on a person also first appeared on the same accounts on Sept. 26, receiving more engagement. That second image also features overlaid text, reading, "Evidence suggests cats have never understood personal space."
(@softcatmemes via Facebook)
Snopes contacted the manager of the accounts to confirm the user created the images with an AI tool. We also asked for the name of the tool and the exact text prompts submitted to create the content. We will update this article if we receive further information.
How we know images are fake
Reverse image searches failed to locate any posts or websites containing the same two images prior to late September. With the ongoing popularity of internet cat content, the idea that no one, until recently, would share supposedly real photos of ancient Egyptian sculptures depicting cats acting silly is unlikely.
As one Reddit user has noted, scans of the images with OpenAI's free tool, that verifies content generated using the company's chatbot, display the results, "This content was generated using OpenAI tools," and, "We found a SynthID watermark that originated from OpenAI." For example, a scan of the image of the cat sitting displays the information shown below.
(via OpenAI)
There is also an inconsistency with one of the shadows in that image. The faint shadow nearest where the photographer is meant to be standing (running from left to right along the long edge of the bed) indicates there is a light source on the other side of the display. However, only a shadow of the bed is cast. If the image were authentic, the angle of the shadow suggests the viewer would also be able to see a faint shadow of the human and cat sculptures. That is not the case in this image.
A scan of the other image of the cat standing or walking displays the same result using OpenAI's tool. The absence of a shadow of the cat's tail also further suggests this image is fake.
For further reading, we previously reported about another feline rumor that wild cheetahs have never killed humans.

Former Australian bishop jailed for sexually abusing young men
- Published
Former Australian bishop Christopher Saunders has been jailed for sexually abusing two young Aboriginal men during his time as a Catholic cleric.
Saunders - who resigned as Bishop of Broome when first accused of wrongdoing in 2020 - was found guilty of one charge of rape and 12 counts of indecent assault in August.
The 76-year-old was on Wednesday sentenced to six and a half years in prison, but will be eligible for release on parole in February 2031.
He is one of the most senior Catholic leaders in the world to face sex abuse charges.
His trial in the state of Western Australia heard Saunders systematically groomed the two young men, inviting them to "shirts-off" gatherings and plying them with alcohol, often using church funds and church-owned properties to do so.
He was convicted of kissing and molesting the men between 2010 and 2019, and in one instance forcing oral sex on one of them.
In a victim impact statement provided to the court, that young man said he still struggled to talk about what had happened.
"I was a toy that he was using," the victim wrote. "My head is pounding now, I'm in so much pain."
"I trusted him. I thought he wanted me to be a better person."
During the trial several child sex abuse charges were discarded, and Saunders was acquitted by the jury of alleged offences against a third young man.
First ordained in 1976, Saunders spent most of his career in the remote Kimberley region in the nation's north-west corner, and was appointed Bishop of Broome in 1996.
The diocese stretches about 770,000 sq km (297,000 sq miles) - an area roughly the size of Turkey - and encompasses some of the most remote parts of the country.
District Court Judge Martin Flynn said Saunders had professed to be an advocate for young Aboriginal men, but instead misused his authority and exploited their vulnerability.
He had "disregarded the dignity" of his victims and caused them lasting harm.
In a statement, Archbishop of Perth Timothy Costelloe said the men who had come forward had shown great courage and resilience in pursuing justice.
"We are sorry for the pain and suffering that was inflicted on you. We are sorry that your trust was so directly and profoundly betrayed by a leader of the church," he said.
"No court sentence can undo the suffering that has been caused or restore all that each person has lost."
The accusations were first aired in 2020, but the initial police investigation that followed was closed without charge.
However after a historic inquiry was ordered by the Pope, police began a new investigation.
Costelloe has previously said the church's investigation into Saunders - paused when police resumed theirs - will restart.
The church is under pressure to strip Saunders of his remaining title and ministry powers, a decision the Archbishop said would be determined by Rome.
Only a handful of "Vos Estis Lux Mundi" - meaning "You Are the Light of the World" in Latin - inquiries have been undertaken around the world.
The investigations are commissioned by the pontiff and were introduced in 2019 to combat sexual abuse and hold bishops and other high-ranking Catholic Church officials accountable for their actions.
Aside from the late Cardinal George Pell, who was jailed and then acquitted, Saunders is the most senior Catholic official in the country to be charged with sex offences.

Student visa

Travis Head has revealed that the fallout from Australia’s 2018 ball-tampering scandal influenced a defining moment early in his captaincy of South Australia, when he shut down a dressing-room discussion about whether the team should tamper with the ball to aid reverse swing.
Head was 24 at the time and on the cusp of becoming a regular in the Australian side. The Newlands scandal had resulted in Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft receiving lengthy suspensions, while Australian cricket was still dealing with the damage to its reputation.
South Australia, meanwhile, had endured five successive seasons at the bottom of the Sheffield Shield table. Against that backdrop, some players reportedly wondered whether the team needed to be more aggressive in preparing the ball, amid suspicions that opponents were still pushing the boundaries.
Head, then South Australia’s captain, made his position clear.
“I made a pretty strong stand at that point,” Head told The Age in Durban. “I just knew what a couple of close friends had gone through, and knew what the [Australian] team had gone through, and the flow-on effect of that.”
For Head, the issue was bigger than results. South Australia could remain at the bottom of the table, he said, but it had to play the game properly.
That attitude has carried into the current Australian team, according to Head. He believes Pat Cummins has helped create an environment in which players are encouraged to treat Test cricket as a game rather than a matter of life and death.
“If South Africa play really, really well, and we lose 3-0, that’s OK; it’s not the end of the world,” Head said.
He also believes Australia benefits from refusing to become consumed by the intense scrutiny surrounding modern Test cricket.
“The storylines of media now is through the roof,” Head said. “So if you can’t enjoy it within the four walls, then you’re never going to.”

(Bloomberg) -- The US Forces in Okinawa paused operations for 48 hours starting at noon on Wednesday and imposed a month-long curfew on military personnel, following the arrest of a US Marine on suspicion of murdering a Japanese woman.
US military personnel on Japan’s southernmost island of Okinawa will cease operations to undergo training on standards and discipline and will be prohibited from leaving their bases to socialize or from consuming alcohol, according to a statement.
“Serving on Okinawa comes with responsibility,” the statement read. “Every interaction with our neighbors either builds or undermines the trust that is essential to our team. When that trust is damaged, it affects the strength of our alliance and the security of this region.”
Following the operational pause, military personnel will be subject to a midnight curfew for a 30-day period, the statement added.
Local police arrested a 20-year-old US serviceman on suspicion of killing 39-year-old Anna Yagi early Saturday at a hotel in the city of Naha. National broadcaster NHK said the serviceman denied the charges, citing police investigators.
The incident threatens to reignite local opposition to the US military presence on Okinawa, where around 30,000 American service members are based.
The rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US troops in 1995 triggered major protests, and serious crimes involving US military personnel since then have periodically stoked opposition to the American military presence on the island.
Ahead of a meeting Wednesday with Okinawa Governor Genta Koja, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi offered condolences to the bereaved family and said her government had lodged a strong protest with Washington. Japan demanded full cooperation with the investigation, strict disciplinary action against US military personnel, thorough measures to prevent a recurrence of such incidents, and appropriate support for the victim’s family, she said.
“As a result, the US side announced new measures,” Takaichi said. “We understand that the US side intends to further scrutinize its code of conduct going forward.”
Koja earlier met with Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi in Tokyo. Ahead of those meetings, Koja said, “This is the result of a failure of human rights training by the US military, given this happened despite repeated requests from the Okinawan side to ensure similar cases are prevented.”
Koja became governor only last month after a campaign in which the long-running dispute over US bases took a back seat to other issues.
“I feel deep frustration that such a heinous and deplorable crime has occurred, and an American serviceman was arrested in connection to it,” Koizumi said. “I hope to push forward discussions between Japan and the US on what measures will be effective in preventing such cases in the future.”

Ahead of Australia’s first ODI against Bangladesh on October 9, Ellyse Perry said it was sad that the national team will not be playing any matches in the upcoming Australian summer.
The Australian women’s team will play six matches in two weeks, finishing with the third T20I against New Zealand on October 22.
After that, Australia will play its next game only in March, which means the number-one ranked team in ODIs and T20Is, will not play an international fixture during its traditional home summer.
“I think everyone at the moment feels the challenge from a scheduling perspective that we’re not able to play probably in the peak months this summer when people are really tuned into cricket. Kids are on holidays, people are off work, so yeah there’s a challenge for sure, because our team has been largely successful and we have got some support from fans around the country,” Perry said.
Unlike the women, the men’s team will play as many as 12 international games during the summer- three ODIs and five T20Is against England from November 13, before a four-Test series against New Zealand from December 9 to January 8.
The summer will also feature the women’s BBL and the WPL, which Perry believes has added to the scheduling challenges.
“We just don’t have enough opportunity to play infront our fans because its a really jam-packed schedule. But hopefully, atleast in the women’s game, we can create more opportunities to play at home,” Perry added.

On 02 October 2026, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held a protest at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park grounds demanding accountability from the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Protesters raised concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleged voter deletions, and transparency in the electoral process. Despite Mumbai Police denying permission for the gathering, thousands attended the protest and raised slogans. Police later registered an FIR against the organisers and 400–500 unidentified participants for allegedly violating restrictions on the assembly.
In this context, a video (here & here) is circulating on social media claiming that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke was attacked at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park during this protest. Let’s verify the claim made in the post.
Claim: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was attacked during a protest at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park on 02 October 2026.
Fact: The video is from 15 June 2026 and shows Abhijeet Dipke being assaulted by unidentified individuals during a youth protest against paper leaks and unemployment in Jaipur, Rajasthan. There are no reports of him being attacked at the Mumbai protest. Hence, the claim made in the post is Misleading.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video shows that the same video (here & here) has been available online since at least 15 June 2026. These posts describe it as Abhijeet Dipke being attacked in Jaipur, Rajasthan.
According to media reports (here, here & here), on 15 June 2026, Dipke was manhandled and slapped multiple times during a youth protest at Shaheed Smarak in Jaipur, Rajasthan. He had reportedly organised the protest to speak out against paper leaks and unemployment, and to demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. As supporters carried Dipke on their shoulders toward the stage, several people emerged from the crowd, pulled him down, and struck his face. This sparked a quick retaliatory scuffle from CJP supporters before the police stepped in and detained the suspects.
Afterwards, Dipke condemned the assault, calling it a sign of fear and cowardice from his opponents. Furthermore, there are no news reports of Dipke being assaulted at the Mumbai Shivaji Park protest
To sum it up, an old video of Abhijeet Dipke being assaulted in Jaipur is falsely shared to claim he was attacked in Mumbai.

A purported screenshot circulated online in fall 2026 of a purported Truth Social post, dated Sept. 22, in which U.S. President Donald Trump wrote that he had "spoken to God" and that "tonight is Armageddon.".
The image spread on multiple platforms, including Instagram, Threads and Facebook. Many commenters appeared to believe Trump actually posted the remarks. The full text of the alleged post read as follows:
I have spoken to God and he has given me a vision of an ocean filled with blood a city of dust a golden throne for me to sit on, eternally!!!, Tonight is Armageddon, the final judgement of good and evil!!!! Lock your doors and do not directly at the flash!!!! God bless us all!!!
President Donald J. Trump
(X user @ZiemowitSzcze11.)
Despite the username matching Trump's real Truth Social username, there's no evidence Trump actually published the post. The earliest version of the image we found appeared on a Polish X account that captioned it (translation via X): "Well, fake, but would you be surprised?" (archived).
We searched Trump's Truth — an online archive of Trump's Truth Social posts — for the word "Armageddon," and none of the three results related to the quote above.
(Trump's Truth)
We also looked all posts Trump actually published on Sept. 22 and found he published four that day. None of the four posts matched the timestamp or content of that in the screenshot.
The fake quote appeared to echo whistleblower reports received by the Military Religious Freedom Foundation that U.S. military commanders told troops their action in Iran was "all part of God's divine plan," allegedly "referring to Armageddon and the imminent return of Jesus Christ."
Trump has echoed similarly apocalyptic language, posting in May 2026, for example, that "a whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again" — referring to U.S. attacks on Iran. He's also faced criticism for his posting an image depicting him in the likeness of Jesus Christ.

Historical figures including the UK’s wartime prime minister Winston Churchill will be replaced on the country’s banknotes by images of an Atlantic puffin, a barn owl, a buff-tailed bumblebee and a European hedgehog, the Bank of England said.
The decision to introduce the animals drew criticism earlier in the year, particularly from right-leaning politicians. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called it “the definition of woke.” 
That’s despite nature having emerged as the most popular theme in a public consultation the Bank held on refreshing its money last year. Among the 44,000 responses to that survey, historical figures ranked third. 
The BOE has proceeded with the plan and this week revealed the four creatures picked following a second consultation that took into account the views of wildlife experts and around half a million members of the public.
“We have chosen four distinct and inspiring animals that not only showcase the great variety of wildlife we have in the UK but will also enhance the security of our banknotes,” said Victoria Cleland, the chief cashier who announced her departure in the summer.
The production of the new notes will also try to make the cash more resistant to counterfeiting. A decision has yet to be made about which animal will adorn which denomination, while the process to introduce new notes will take a “few years,” the Bank said.
Churchill has been on the £5 note for the last decade, while other notes feature the author Jane Austen, painter JMW Turner and Second World War code-breaker Alan Turing. On the reverse side all notes show the monarch King Charles III.

A video showing a group of people marching on a road while waving Bangladesh’s national flags is being shared on social media (here, here, and here) with claims that it shows illegal migrants raising Bangladeshi flags in Virar, Maharashtra. Some social media users have also linked the video to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, suggesting that the visuals highlight the need for the exercise. Let’s verify the truth behind the video in this article.
Claim: The video shows illegal migrants raising Bangladeshi flags in Virar, Maharashtra.
Fact: The viral video does not show illegal migrants raising Bangladeshi flags in Virar, Maharashtra. It shows participants carrying Bangladeshi flags during a Hero bike advertisement shoot in Virar on 03 October 2026. Prakash Kawale, Senior Police Inspector at Bolinj Police Station, confirmed to Factly that the video was from the shoot. Dinesh Jaiswal, owner of DJ Location, the production house involved, also confirmed this, adding that the shoot was cancelled after a ruckus and that all the participants were Indian. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
Upon closely reviewing the viral video, we noticed several details that raised questions about its authenticity. A mounted camera is visible at the beginning of the video and again around the 12-second mark. A cloth diffuser, typically used to control lighting during a shoot, is also visible. These details indicate that the footage was recorded during a shoot.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to multiple media reports (here, here, and here) featuring similar visuals. According to these reports, a Bangladeshi flag was used during a commercial advertisement shoot in Virar, a suburb in Maharashtra’s Palghar district, which triggered protests from local groups. The reports noted that some locals complained to the police and later burned the Bangladeshi flags used by the production crew. One of the reports also captured the aftermath, showing several youths attempting to burn a Bangladeshi flag.
We contacted Mr Prakash Kawale, Senior Police Inspector at Bolinj Police Station in Virar, regarding the viral video. Speaking to Factly, he confirmed that the video was recorded during an advertisement shoot. According to him, “This was an ad shoot by a Hero Bike company on 03 October 2026.”
We also learnt from the inspector that the shoot was carried out by DJ Location. We also contacted Dinesh Jaiswal, the owner of the production house, who confirmed that the video was recorded during an advertisement shoot for a Hero bike. He said the shoot was cancelled after a ruckus broke out, following which the concept was dropped. He added that all the people involved in the shoot were Indian and clarified that the video was from an advertisement shoot, not a real incident involving illegal migrants.
To sum up, this viral video does not show illegal migrants raising Bangladeshi flags in Virar, Maharashtra; it is from an advertisement shoot.

24 luxury houses at One Stanley sold amid probe into alleged construction defects
Experts call for stronger homebuyer protections, including mandatory period for buyers to rescind purchase contracts
Around two dozen luxury houses at One Stanley have been sold since Hong Kong authorities launched an investigation into alleged structural defects in March, with buyers including local and international businesspeople.
These transactions have prompted experts to call for stronger homebuyer protections, including implementing a mandatory period for buyers to rescind contracts when statutory violations are discovered.

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant agreed on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) to urgently hear a Union government plea that the State of Jharkhand is appointing Directors General of Police (DGPs) in defiance of a series of judicial orders passed by the Supreme Court since the past 20 years.
The Union government, through the Home Ministry, has also sought a judicial declaration that the ‘Selection and Appointment of Director General and Inspector General of Police, Jharkhand (Head of Police), Regulation of 2025’ be declared ultra vires the apex court’s Prakash Singh versus Union of India judgment of 2006. The application has sought a direction to the State of Jharkhand to company with the Prakash Singh judgment, and further declare the appointments of DGPs pursuant to the 2025 Regulation as illegal.

Attackers hijacked three top-level domains and used their control to mint counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large organizations, Google said Tuesday.
The attackers launched a series of attacks on the .gh, .sl, and .as country code top-level domains (ccTLDs) and then modified authoritative DNS records for selected domains within those namespaces. By controlling those DNS records, the attackers were able to pass automated domain control validation checks and obtain unauthorized certificates for “several Google domains” and “several leading global brands and widely used online services.” Google said it updated Chrome to block all certificates it identified as unauthorized, and worked with the issuing certification authorities to ensure the unauthorized certificates for Google properties were revoked.
Certificate issuance: The weak link in the chain
TLS certificates are the cryptographic credentials that underpin authentication and encryption protections for websites, mail servers, and other Internet infrastructure. These x.509 certificates use a digital signature to bind a domain name such as google.com to a public key. The public key is publicly available, while the private key is held only by the website operator. When a connection shows that the keys match, the visiting party knows it’s connected to the authentic site rather than an impostor. Possession of unauthorized certificates allows attackers to cryptographically impersonate the affected infrastructure.
Google didn’t identify the affected domains it owns or name any of the other organizations whose domains were affected. While noting that Chrome users do not need to take any action to be protected, Google cautioned domain owners not to rely solely on browser-side interventions to protect their users. The company is advising domain owners to monitor certificate transparency logs for unexpected certificate issuance across their domains and to publish restrictive Certification Authority Authorization DNS records to prevent attackers from reusing cached validation data after DNS control is restored.

Calm in real life but demons on court - Medvedev runs out of chances
- Published
Daniil Medvedev once said you would need to knock on his hotel door at 6am for seven days in a row to make him angry.
On court, though, he is a far more combustible character who finally ran out of chances when he was disqualified from Monday's China Open semi-final against Novak Djokovic.
Djokovic was serving for a place in the final when the ball ricocheted off the back of the court. Medvedev swiped it into the stands, where it hit a spectator in the face.
A few minutes later the Russian was defaulted, as he had to be, under rules that bar a player from "hitting a ball dangerously or recklessly, or with negligent disregard of the consequences."
Players have got away with worse. There is sometimes anger in their actions, but it is rarely of the bulging-neck-vein variety.
It is more often a sign of irritation and petulance, with frustrations taken out on the ball with little care for the safety of officials, ball kids and the spectators who line the court.
"I can only say I'm a really calm person in life - I actually have no idea why the demons go out when I play tennis," Medvedev said at the 2019 US Open, where he was fined for snatching a towel from a ball person and making an offensive gesture to fans inside the Arthur Ashe Stadium.
"Especially when I was a junior, I had a lot of problems with my attitude.
"I was not getting defaulted, but to have a game penalty was easy."
Returning to the theme at that year's end-of-season ATP Finals, Medvedev said any bad blood soon disappears after leaving the court.
"All my temper goes away after I leave the tennis court. If I'm not happy with my practice, I step out of the court and five minutes later, I'm OK," he said.
It is hard - and probably unwise - to take your eyes off Medvedev's matches, and he is very popular with the media for his engaging, reflective and humorous interviews once the dust has settled.
But he has gone too far on court on many occasions, with much of his aggression directed at umpires.
At Wimbledon in 2017, a 21-year-old Medvedev was so incensed about some of the decisions made by umpire Mariana Alves in his second-round match that he sprinkled coins at her feet as she climbed down from the chair.
He later apologised and denied he was accusing her of bias.
Two years ago, again at Wimbledon, it appeared officials were considering defaulting Medvedev for an outburst towards umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore.
Medvedev claimed he said something in Russian which was "not pleasant, but not over the line" - and, after a discussion between the umpire, supervisor and tournament referee, he escaped with a code violation for unsportsmanlike conduct.
He was fined more than £60,000 for his behaviour at the 2025 Australian Open, which included trying to destroy a net camera, and had an infamous meltdown later that year at the US Open.
On a rowdy New York night, Benjamin Bonzi had match point for a straight-set win against Medvedev in the first round when a photographer inexplicably walked on to court between his first and second serves.
Umpire Greg Allensworth awarded the Frenchman another first serve because of the delay, sparking fury from Medvedev.
Medvedev accused Allensworth of hoping to engineer a quick finish - as he gets paid by the match, rather than the hour - and there was a pause of over five minutes as he whipped up the crowd.
He did save the match point, but went on to lose in five sets before obliterating his racquet by smashing it repeatedly against the table next to his chair.
Medvedev will lose all the prize money and ranking points he earned from his run to the semi-finals in Beijing. He remains in the eighth and final qualifying spot for November's ATP Finals, but the loss of 200 points could yet prove crucial.
The 30-year-old has apologised for his actions and said he hopes to say sorry to the spectator in person.
In New York a month ago, Medvedev reflected on the role of genetics when explaining how his eldest daughter has "my personality on the court".
"She plays a bit. She enjoys it. Maybe it's a bit of a genetic somewhere there," Medvedev added.
"I took her to practice once. She's happy, so she throws the racquet through the whole court.
"The coach looks at me and says: 'I don't know where she got this from...'
"All the people that talk about that I should control myself more - she's three years old. It's not like we taught her to do the things she's doing on the court."
