Eight Muslim women from Vijayapura have alleged that they were wrongly shown as “deceased” in documents submitted to the Election Commission of India (ECI) as part of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Karnataka. They demanded that a criminal case be registered against Vijayapura MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal, expelled from the BJP, and those responsible for submitting the alleged bogus death certificates.
The women made the allegations at a press conference by Jagrutha Karnataka, a social-political organisation, here on Wednesday. They also displayed copies of the death certificates and other documents which, they claimed, had been used to show them as dead.
Representatives of the organisation alleged Mr. Yatnal had submitted the list in a letter dated August 31, a week after the publication of the draft electoral rolls on August 24. The organisation questioned how the names of voters across 198 polling stations could have been matched with details of deceased persons within such a short period.
It also questioned how colour photographs from voter ID cards accompanying the list had been obtained, alleging that such photographs were available in the ECI records.
The ‘deceased’ women
Raziya Sheikh, anganwadi helper and resident of Vijayapura city for nearly 30 years, said she was illiterate and was working to support her family. “A certificate has been submitted claiming that I am dead. I am worried that I may lose my ration card and other government benefits,” she said.
Ms. Raziya Sheikh and seven other Muslim women residing in Vijayapura had been shown as “deceased”. Mahaboobi Sheikh and Malani Jamadar, who spoke on behalf of the other women, urged the ECI to register FIRs against officials who allegedly issued false death certificates and those who submitted them to the Commission.
The women alleged that an attempt was being made to deprive them of their right to vote because they were Muslims.
Criminal action sought
Jagrutha Karnataka convener H.V. Vasu alleged Mr. Yatnal had submitted a list of 1,054 persons, but death certificates had been attached in only eight cases.
According to Mr. Vasu, discrepancies in the names and the names of husbands or fathers in the documents had resulted in living persons such as Ms. Jamadar, Ms. Mahaboobi Sheikh, and Ms. Raziya Sheikh being shown as dead.
Mr. Vasu also alleged that election officials had acted swiftly after the MLA submitted his letter and demanded that a criminal case be registered against Mr. Yatnal.
Claim over Form 7 applications
Irfan Sheikh, local journalist from Vijayapura, alleged that a total of 13,000 printed Form 7 applications had been submitted to the municipal authorities in two batches of 5,000 and 8,000.
He claimed that the applications were withdrawn on the same evening after the ECI sought an endorsement relating to the self-declaration accompanying the applications. He alleged that the withdrawal was an attempt to prevent the alleged irregularities from coming to light.

బ్యాంకులకు వారానికి ఐదు రోజుల పని విధానం అమలు చేయాలని బ్యాంకు ఉద్యోగ సంఘాలు చాలా కాలంగా డిమాండ్ చేస్తున్నాయి. ఈ డిమాండ్పై సెప్టెంబర్ 2026లో యునైటెడ్ ఫోరం ఆఫ్ బ్యాంక్ యూనియన్స్ (UFBU) దేశవ్యాప్తంగా నిరసనలు చేపట్టింది. వీటిలో పెన్షన్ ప్రయోజనాలను మెరుగుపరచడం, పాత పెన్షన్ విధానాన్ని (OPS) తిరిగి అమలు చేయడం, పెండింగ్లో ఉన్న వేతన సమస్యలను పరిష్కరించడం వంటి డిమాండ్లు ఉన్నాయి. సెప్టెంబర్ 2026 చివర్లో మూడు రోజుల బ్యాంకు సమ్మెకు పిలుపునిచ్చారు. అయితే, ఇండియన్ బ్యాంక్స్ అసోసియేషన్ ఈ అంశాలపై చర్చించేందుకు అంగీకరించడంతో సమ్మెను వాయిదా వేశారు.
ఈ నేపథ్యంలో, ఆర్థిక మంత్రిత్వ శాఖ జారీ చేసినట్లు చెబుతున్న ఒక గెజిట్ నోటిఫికేషన్ సోషల్ మీడియాలో (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) వైరల్ అవుతోంది. ఇందులో అన్ని ప్రభుత్వ రంగ బ్యాంకులకు ప్రతి శనివారం సెలవు ఉంటుందని, ఈ నిబంధన వెంటనే అమల్లోకి వస్తుందని కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం ప్రకటించినట్లు పేర్కొన్నారు. ఈ పోస్ట్లో చేసిన వాదనను ఇప్పుడు పరిశీలిద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: ప్రభుత్వ రంగ బ్యాంకులకు ప్రతి శనివారం సెలవు ఉంటుందని ఆర్థిక మంత్రిత్వ శాఖ జారీ చేసిన గెజిట్ నోటిఫికేషన్.
ఫాక్ట్: PIB ఫ్యాక్ట్ చెక్ ప్రకారం, ఆర్థిక మంత్రిత్వ శాఖ ఇలాంటి నోటిఫికేషన్ను ఏదీ జారీ చేయలేదు. సోషల్ మీడియాలో వైరల్ అవుతున్న గెజిట్ నోటిఫికేషన్ OpenAI టూల్స్ను ఉపయోగించి AI ద్వారా రూపొందించినది. కాబట్టి, ఈ పోస్ట్లో చేసిన వాదన తప్పు.
ముందుగా, ఇలాంటి నోటిఫికేషన్ ఏదైనా విడుదలైందా అని తెలుసుకోవడానికి ప్రభుత్వం యొక్క అధికారిక e-Gazette పోర్టల్ను పరిశీలించాము. అయితే, అక్కడ దీనికి సంబంధించిన ఎలాంటి రికార్డు కనిపించలేదు. అలాగే, ఈ విషయంపై భారత ప్రభుత్వం నుంచి ఎలాంటి అధికారిక ప్రకటన కూడా వెలువడలేదు.
తర్వాత, వైరల్గా మారిన గెజిట్ నోటిఫికేషన్ చిత్రాన్ని OpenAI కంటెంట్ డిటెక్షన్ టూల్ను ఉపయోగించి పరిశీలించాము. ఈ పరిశీలనలో, ఈ గెజిట్ నోటిఫికేషన్ OpenAI టూల్స్ను ఉపయోగించి AI ద్వారా రూపొందించినట్లు తేలింది.
అదనంగా, ప్రభుత్వ ప్రెస్ ఇన్ఫర్మేషన్ బ్యూరో (PIB) ఫ్యాక్ట్ చెక్ ఈ విషయంపై స్పష్టత (ఆర్కైవ్) ఇచ్చింది. ప్రభుత్వ రంగ బ్యాంకులకు ప్రతి శనివారం సెలవు ప్రకటిస్తూ ఆర్థిక మంత్రిత్వ శాఖ ఎలాంటి నోటిఫికేషన్ జారీ చేయలేదని సోషల్ మీడియాలో వైరల్ అవుతున్న గెజిట్ నోటిఫికేషన్ నకిలీదని నిర్ధారించింది.
చివరిగా, వైరల్ అవుతున్న గెజిట్ నోటిఫికేషన్ AI ద్వారా రూపొందించబడింది; అన్ని శనివారాలను బ్యాంకులకు సెలవులుగా ప్రభుత్వం ప్రకటించలేదు.

Rahm to leave LIV Golf over 'unacceptable' terms
- Published
Jon Rahm will leave LIV Golf after deeming the proposed terms for LIV 2.0 "unacceptable", his lawyer has told a bankruptcy court hearing.
The league, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabia withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding, has secured a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to try to move forward with the 2027 season.
Rahm's lawyer, John Beck, told the hearing the 31-year-old Spaniard "independently reviewed the terms of LIV 2.0 and determined those terms are unacceptable as to him".
It was later said that LIV and Rahm's representatives are "in advanced discussions for a consensual separation agreement between Mr Rahm and LIV".
It is hoped this will be finalised by a court hearing on 5 November.
LIV's participants are owed at least $45m (£33m) and have the option to leave.
However, the agreement secures an extension for the league to discuss terms with its players, with talks now open until 25 October.
Documents outlining the money owed to LIV Golf's creditors, with the 30 largest unsecured claims, show that two-time major winner Rahm tops the list with an unsecured claim of $7.5m (£5.5m).
BBC Sport understands there is no obligation on players to sign on to LIV 2.0, regardless of whether they had previously signed multi-year contracts with LIV Golf.
Spain's Rahm was arguably the most high-profile name to join LIV when he left the PGA Tour in December 2023 for a deal worth a reported £222m ($300m).
Some players, including Brooks Koepka, have since returned to the PGA Tour, which rewrote its rules in December to allow the five-time major winner to come back, subject to certain sanctions.
Rahm did not follow suit and remained under long-term contract with LIV, but in May reached a deal with the DP World Tour - formerly the European Tour - to retain his membership and remain eligible for next year's Ryder Cup.
LIV golfers are automatically banned for a year by the PGA Tour. The DP World Tour offers a pathway because the leading 10 players on the European circuit currently gain access to PGA Tour membership.
In August, former world number one Rahm won his third straight LIV season title.
He has previously said he had no regrets over joining LIV and backed organisers to make it sustainable.
Chapter 11 protection postpones a US company's obligations to its creditors, giving it time to reorganise its debts or sell parts of the business.
Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) is providing a bankruptcy loan of $49.6m (£36.6m) - called 'debtor in possession' (DIP) financing - to help fund the process.

Meanwhile, former Masters champion Sergio Garcia was granted a special "deal" during Wednesday's hearing in New Jersey allowing his contract to be "terminated" as well as "rejected", following an application by his lawyers.
Once that termination agreement is signed, it is understood Garcia will be free to negotiate with third parties.
Earlier he had told media at the Open de Espana in Madrid how keen he is to be involved in next year's Ryder Cup as a player or vice-captain.
While he said that he was not sure what his future held and "everything is an option", he made clear he wanted to give himself "the best chance" of making the Ryder Cup team.
Lawyers for several other players, including Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith, also spoke in the hearing to seek clarity on whether the rejection of the contracts equated to termination of the contracts.
One lawyer, representing five players including Smith, said clarity was needed on whether players could engage in discussions about "future plans with third parties".
The likely background to this is that players want to know for certain whether they are legally permitted to hold discussions with rival tours and also sponsors.
The DP World Tour, for example, is understood to be unwilling to have discussions with LIV players surrounding their futures unless they have proof that their contracts have been terminated.
There was no indication given regarding these players' positions in relation to LIV 2.0.
However, lawyers representing LIV did not agree to apply the same arrangement that Garcia had received, instead asking for more time to assess player contracts and the consequences of termination.
Keith Martorana, counsel for LIV Golf, said: "We are not looking to hold anybody up unduly but we have unfortunately at this point had no opportunity to review those contracts."
This matter has therefore been pushed back to a hearing on 14 October.
LIV insiders remain positive about the future, saying conversations with players are on track and the statements made in court have not changed the momentum behind the transaction.
Ted Goldthorpe, head of BC Partners Credit, told BBC Sport on Tuesday he was "confident" they would get the required number and calibre of players to sign up for LIV 2.0 by the new deadline of 25 October.
"The next focus for us is going to be to sign players, which we're going to work on for the next month. In parallel to that, we're going to be business planning, event planning, rehiring the staff, you know, and revitalising the LIV. I'm spending a lot of time on this right now."
Asked about conversations with players, he said: "I'm not that worried, I'm honestly not that worried about it. I don't think we have a hard deadline for a number of players or who those players are. But we feel pretty confident we have critical mass."
He added that BC Partners was wanting to be involved with LIV for the "long-term".

The Trump administration is facing growing questions over its decision to abandon a fraud and bribery case against the Indian billionaire Gautam Adani after he promised to invest $10bn in the US.
For the second time this year, two Democratic senators have demanded attorney general Todd Blanche answer questions about the US Department of Justice department’s handling of the case – and raised concerns over its judgment under Donald Trump.
In August, a federal judge in New York agreed to drop the fraud case against Adani, one of the richest people in the world, at the request of prosecutors, despite having concerns about “irregularities” in the “highly unusual” decision. It has become the latest example of judges raising eyebrows at Trump administration prosecutors for pushing to dismiss criminal cases.
Now, more than a month later, senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal are asking Blanche to clarify whether people close to Donald Trump were involved in that decision.
It comes aftera New York Times report revealed that Adani, represented by one of Trump’s personal lawyers, admitted to offering a $10bn investment in the US to resolve the criminal case. The federal judge overseeing the case determined the investment played no role in the DoJ’s decision to abandon the case.
“These fresh details continue to raise concerns about the judgment of the DoJ, and the extent to which the DoJ is willing and able to prosecute white-collar criminals under President Trump,” Warren and Blumenthal wrote in a letter sent on Wednesday, and seen by the Guardian.
Adani was indicted in 2024 in New York for allegedly participating in a bribery and fraud scheme in which he paid Indian officials to secure a contract for one of his companies. He denied the allegations.
Prosecutors suddenly moved to dismiss the case against Adani in May after he hired a new legal team, led by Robert Giuffra Jr, and offered to invest $10bn into the US.
Following the news, Warren and Blumenthal sent a letter to Blanche in June requesting information about the fraud case and raising concerns about whether the justice department dismissed the case in exchange for Adani’s investment.
However, the senators did not receive a response. Since then, new details about the case have emerged, including allegations that Boris Epshteyn, a member of Trump’s personal legal team who also served as an informal adviser, helped Adani.
Another report claimed Donald Trump Jr, the president’s son, met with Adani in November 2025, before the case was dropped. A spokesperson for Trump Jr said earlier this year that the conversation “had zero to do with DoJ’s actions in this case”.
A spokesperson for Epshteyn denied being involved in Adani’s “arguments, advocacy or efforts” to the Wall Street Journal in June. Epshteyn was never hired by Adani or his company, the Adani Group, nor did he maintain a relationship with Adani, the spokesperson added.
The Guardian has asked Epshteyn for comment.
The Democratic lawmakers are now asking the DoJ for more information about Adani’s alleged investment offer, including a list of employees who were present when the offer was made, the terms of the offer, when the offer was made and where.
They also want to know whether the DoJ employees knew Epshteyn was allegedly working on behalf of Adani, or if Epshteyn had any contact with DoJ employees regarding Adani, among other questions.
“We are also concerned about the involvement of two of President Trump’s personal lawyers in this case, and the extent to which they reveal potential political influence and special treatment for well-connected insiders at the DoJ,” Warren and Blumenthal wrote in their letter.
The Democrats also want to know if Trump Jr, or any person working on behalf of Trump Jr., had contact with a DoJ employee regarding Adani.
Warren and Blumenthal requested responses no later than 5 October. The Guardian has asked Blanche’s office for comment.

Is it too early to look at Premier League table?
- Published
Just five games in, it might seem a bit early to pay much attention to the Premier League table - but it's probably more settled than you think.
While it would be no surprise if Manchester City and Arsenal finish as the top two -outside of any points deductions or sanctions directed City's way - will Brentford really qualify for Europe, Hull stay up and Tottenham be involved in yet another relegation battle? Recent history certainly suggests it's likely.
It has to be mentioned there is a huge asterisk hanging over the Premier League table at the moment after Man City were found guilty of the majority of the Premier League charges levelled at them.
The Premier League leaders have appealed but, if the guilty verdict remains, potential sanctions could have a significant impact on the table. Until then, we can only deal with the table as it is now.
If we look at the Premier League after five games last season and where teams ultimately ended up, the final table was already starting to take shape as 13 of the 20 sides finished within four places of where they sat even at this early stage (65%).
Eventual champions Arsenal were second, Sunderland were already seventh ahead of finishing there eight months later, and two of the three sides that were relegated were already in the bottom three.
There were some notable exceptions. Aston Villa and Tottenham effectively swapped places at either end of the table, with Villa rising up from the bottom three to finish in the top four and Spurs dropping to 17th.
It's a similar story across the last 10 seasons of the Premier League. Over two-thirds of teams finished within four places of where they were after five games (138 out of 200), with 27 of those sitting in exactly the same position 33 games later.
Another 50 teams finished between five and nine places from where they were at this stage, meaning that just 12 teams in the last decade moved up or down the table by double digits after this point, with three of those coming last season.
However, one part of the table that doesn't settle quickly is the top spot. The side leading the Premier League after five games has gone on to win the title in just one of the last six seasons – Man City doing so in 2023-24 – and just three times in the last 11 seasons.
Even the fact that Man City have five wins out of five so far doesn't mean much. They also won their first five games under Manuel Pellegrini in 2015-16 and in Pep Guardiola's first season in 2016-17 but didn't go on to win the title on either occasion (although they did in 2023-24).
Chelsea in 2018-19, Arsenal in 2022-23 and Liverpool last season were also top with a 100% record at this stage but had little to show for it at the end of the season.
However, the eventual champions have been in the top two at this point in each of the last four campaigns, suggesting - potential punishments aside - it will be Man City or Arsenal that lifts the trophy. The last team to be outside the top two after five games and win the title were Man City in 2021-22, who were fifth with just 10 points.
The top end of the table overall has sometimes settled surprisingly quickly in recent years. The top eight after five games in 2024-25 finished as the top eight at the end of that season (although not in the same order), while the top six in 2019-20 and top seven in 2016-17 were also in place at this early stage.
While being top after five games hasn't meant much in recent seasons, being bottom certainly has.
After finishing just one place above the drop in the last two campaigns, Tottenham could well be in trouble once again as the side bottom of the Premier League after five games has been relegated in six of the last seven seasons.
Being bottom this early didn't used to be such a bad omen. Between 2013-14 and 2018-19, only one of the six sides that were propping up the table after five games ended up going down – Newcastle in 2015-16 – while Crystal Palace finished as high as 11th in 2017-18.
In fact, the good news for Tottenham fans is that the last time they were in this situation, they finished eighth. The club were bottom with just two points after five games in 2008-09 but, after replacing manager Juande Ramos with Harry Redknapp three games later, still finished in the top half.
Looking at the relegation battle more broadly, at least one of the teams in the bottom three at this stage has been relegated in the last eight seasons - so one of Tottenham, Fulham and Coventry will very likely be heading to the Championship in May.
The pool of contestants for this season's relegation battle may already be decided too as the three sides that ultimately went down in the last three seasons were all in the bottom six after five games, which would add Bournemouth, Aston Villa and Crystal Palace to the mix.
The last sides to be outside the bottom six at this point but relegated were Leeds and Southampton in 2022-23, who were both in the top half (7th and 9th). With their teams currently sat in 8th and 11th place, Hull and Ipswich fans will hope that's still the case at the end of this campaign.
While the season may well have barely begun, the Premier League table is already starting to take shape.

The Keralam government has constituted a high-level task force to develop an evidence-based road map for a phased prevention and early detection framework, along with appropriate treatment and rehabilitation plan, and an action plan for healthy ageing, with the broader objective of establishing a “Kerala Holistic Model for Health, Wellness and Longevity”.
According to the government order issued by the Health and Family Welfare department on Wednesday, the task force will be headed by the Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, with Health Minister K. Muraleedharan as vice-chairman. Sharmila Mary Joseph, Principal Secretary (Health and Family Welfare and AYUSH), will be the member-coordinator.
The 16-member task force includes K.R. Jyothilal, Additional Chief Secretary (Finance); Ratan Kelkar, Secretary to the Chief Minister; Deepak Singhal, former Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary; Shiv Kumar Sarin, Director of Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences, New Delhi; Faizal E Kottikolon, chairman, KEF Holdings; C. Devidas Varier, managing director of AVP Coimbatore; Harsh Mahajan, chairman of Mahajan Imaging and Labs; Pratap Chauhan, chairman Jive Ayurva; Kancherioa Ravindranath, chairman, Global Hospital, Hyderabad; S.S. Lal, Director ReAct Asia Pacific; P.M. Varier, chief physician, Arya Vaidya Sala Kottakkal; M.V. Pillai, chairman International Cancer Care Network, USA, and Nisha Nigil, President-elect, Association of Kerala Medical Graduates in North America.
The task force has been asked first to assess Keralam’s disease burden, ageing trends, healthcare service capacity and gaps in access, and identify priority populations, diseases and districts.
Path forward
It will then design a phased prevention and early-detection framework covering risk assessment, screening protocols, referral pathways, follow-up and measurable coverage targets, aligned with existing State and national programmes.
A significant component of its mandate is to explore and identify evidence-based models for coordination among modern medicine, Ayurveda and other recognised systems of medicine. The order specifically calls for clearly defined scopes of practice, clinical governance, consent, contraindications, referral mechanisms and adverse-event reporting.
The task force will also examine the creation of a network of diagnostic, hospital, rehabilitation and wellness services, including criteria for pilot projects, accreditation, quality assurance and independent evaluation.
Another proposed component is the implementation of a Keralam Health Intelligence and Longevity Grid, with emphasis on interoperability with existing health systems, consent, privacy, cybersecurity and data stewardship.
Its mandate extends to workforce development in nursing, allied health, public health and relevant systems of medicine. It will also set uop research partnerships in health economics and financing.
The task force has been asked to examine possible investment and public-private partnership (PPP) models for diagnostics and wellness infrastructure, specifying fiscal exposure, procurement safeguards and public benefit.
It will also examine standards and opportunities for health and wellness tourism and identify the legal, regulatory and institutional changes required to implement its recommendations.
The order also recommends facilitation and support of the proposed World Holistic Health Forum, “a global NGO”, after assessing its purpose, financial commitment and expected outcomes so that Kerala’s positioning as a “cradle and destination” for holistic health, wellness and longevity can be explored.
Action-oriented report
The task force is required to submit an action-oriented report within two months of its first meeting.
The report is expected to contain a baseline assessment and priorities, two or three defined pilot projects with details; a three-year phased roadmap, indicative costs and funding sources and fiscal risks.
The task force is also expected to draft institutional and regulatory measures, and an implementation dashboard specifying milestones and accountable departments.
The Health and Family Welfare department will function as the nodal department, with support from AYUSH, Finance and other departments. Research, analytical, financial, technical and secretarial personnel will be deputed from the Health Department and its attached organisations.

Canada’s federal government said on Wednesday it would advance legislation to prevent people whose sole health condition is mental illness from accessing euthanasia, an effort by the ruling Liberal party to address a clash in the country over who has access to physician-assisted death.
Under the current rules, people whose sole underlying medical condition is a mental illness have been barred from accessing medical assistance in dying (Maid) to end their lives. But that ban – due to be lifted in March – has divided lawmakers over whether to permit this expansion of the Maid program.
Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, the justice minister, Sean Fraser, said his government would indefinitely bar people whose sole condition is mental illness from accessing the program. He said that while there was no “perfect consensus” on this issue, upcoming legislation reflected the “correct” approach.
Earlier this year, a government committee concluded the government should expand access to Maid and should “indefinitely exclude persons whose sole underlying medical condition is a mental illness from eligibility for medical assistance in dying”. That report also flagged the need for “increased and more equitable access” to mental health services.
Canada’s Maid laws, drawn up after a 2015 supreme court decision, initially only permitted those who are terminally ill to be eligible for the procedure. But in 2019, a Quebec judge ruled that restricting access to those who had a “reasonably foreseeable death” was unconstitutional, forcing federal lawmakers to amend and expand the existing laws.
In 2021, the law was updated so adults could receive an assisted death if two doctors confirmed an irremediable physical condition causing immense suffering that cannot be relieved. Given the uncertainty surrounding mental illness, lawmakers in 2021 initially put a temporary exclusion in place for people who suffer solely from a mental illness. They renewed that pause in 2023 and 2024.
According to the latest government figures, the vast majority of Maid deaths – 95.6% – involved people whose natural death was considered “reasonably foreseeable”. Only 4.4% were cases in which death was not considered reasonably foreseeable. Those include people with conditions such as multiple sclerosis and incurable neurological disease that can causes profound disability and immense suffering.
The Liberal party’s legislation is also an effort to ward off a private member’s bill that would amend the section of the criminal code covering Maid so that “a mental disorder is not a grievous and irremediable medical condition”.
Advocates for expanding Maid to include mental illness alone say the current rules violate their constitutional rights and access to healthcare. Fraser acknowledged to reporters that a federal case – led by the advocacy group Dying With Dignity Canada – challenging the government’s previous decision to delay access to Maid for people with mental illness could affect the upcoming bill.
Fraser said lawmakers would also work to decriminalize what are known as advanced requests, effectively giving people suffering from some illnesses such as Alzheimer’s the chance to choose Maid before their illness deprives them of the capacity to consent.
At present, Quebec is the only jurisdiction that permits the use of these requests. Fraser gave no specifics on the timing of the legislation but said that provinces will decide whether to provide advance requests. While the province of Alberta has already said it will not permit advance requests, the justice minister said the bill attempts to ensure “the doctors who provide the services will not be treated as criminals for doing so”.

Bharatiya Kishan Union Leader Rakesh Tikait on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) raised questions over Satellite Township Projects in Bihar, asserting that the Union will not allow farmers’ land and rights to be compromised in the name of development.
Bihar government has prepared a blueprint for 11 satellite townshipss across 10 districts of Bihar. These townships will feature planned residential colonies, designated commercial areas, wide roads, and green spaces with plantations along roadsides and in parks.
Addressing a press conference in Patna, Mr. Tikait said that a review of this entire model suggests that unless transparency, social impact assessment, fair compensation, rehabilitation, and farmers’ consent are ensured in time, it could lead to the large-scale transfer of agricultural land and the promotion of land speculation under the guise of development.
He asserted that the Union is not opposed to development; however, development that comes at the cost of farmers losing their land, livelihoods, and social security cannot be accepted.
The Bihar government has announced plans to develop large-scale satellite townships in Patna, Darbhanga, Saran , Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Muzaffarpur, Gaya, Purnia, Sitamarhi, Munger, and Saharsa, in which lakhs of acres of land are being identified for these projects.
He pointed out that there are several significant objections in the Bihar Town Development Act, 2026, and the Act proposes granting excessive powers for the establishment, development, control, and management of cities.
“How will the new law uphold the protective provisions—regarding farmers’ interests, social impact assessment, consent, rehabilitation, and compensation—that already exist under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (RFCTLARR Act, 2013), and the Bihar Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Rules, 2014,” Mr. Tikait asked.
He added, “Farmers’ land cannot be viewed merely as land for urban development; for a farmer, land is not just an asset but a source of livelihood, social security, and the economic foundation for future generations.”
Land pooling
Mr. Tikait mentioned that there are several questions surrounding the land pooling system, while the proposal involves acquiring farmers’ land and returning a portion of it to a developed State.
He asked, on what basis the returned land will be valued and what will be the location and quality of the land allocated to the farmer. He also asked what rights the farmer will have over that land. He added that in any land pooling arrangement, the farmer should be treated not merely as a land provider but as a genuine partner in the development process.
Mr. Tikait claimed that the law lacks a clear formula or specific mention regarding compensation in exchange for land. He also pointed out that the new law makes no provision for social audits or social impact assessments.
“If the government wishes to modernise Bihar, it is welcome to do so. However, a modern Bihar cannot mean making fertile village land available for large real estate projects. If agricultural land is gradually converted into real estate markets under the guise of satellite townships, the greatest loss will be borne by farmers and rural society,” Mr. Tikait said.
He informed that during the COVID-19 pandemic crisis, a large number of people returned from cities to their villages, where the village and the land served as a foundation of security.
Key demands
He demanded that the Bihar Town Development Act, 2026, be scrapped and that Social Impact Assessments and Social Audits be made mandatory for every project.
He urged to refrain from diluting the farmer-friendly provisions of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, regarding land acquisition and compensation. Also provide a legal guarantee over the land, its value, and the rights of farmers under land pooling schemes.
“A transparent pricing mechanism should be established to bridge the gap between circle rates and actual market values. Information regarding all proposals, land area, master plans, and land-use details concerning satellite townships should be made public,” Mr. Tikait added.
He warned that if these demands are not met within a month, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha and all farmers’ organisations in Bihar will organise a massive farmers’ march in Patna in November 2026, where farmers will stage a sit-in protest until this law is withdrawn.

'Draining' few days for Gauff after online racist abuse
- Published
Coco Gauff said she had a "draining" few days after receiving racist abuse online before her fourth-round China Open exit.
The American received an "insane" amount of racist comments and direct messages following an incident in her third-round win over 16-year-old Sun Xinran on Monday.
China's Sun thought she had hit a winner late in the first set, but Gauff raised her hand to halt play because of a flickering light in the side panels surrounding the court.
After a video review - which players are allowed to request - the point was replayed, with Gauff winning it and subsequently going on to clinch the match.
The 22-year-old posted a lengthy statement explaining what had happened and later condemned the racist abuse she received in response.
Gauff was beaten 6-3 6-3 in her next match against Elise Mertens on Wednesday.
Asked how she had felt over the past 36 hours, Gauff said: "It has been kind of draining, I'm not going to lie.
"I just turn off my phone and move on. I mean, there's nothing you can do."
A spokesperson for the Women's Tennis Association said it was appalled by the abuse. It said it was in contact with Gauff "to offer our full support".
A statement given to the news agency AFP said the governing body was "seeking action" against the abusive content.
Gauff, who won the title in Beijing in 2024, committed 34 unforced errors and eight double faults against Mertens.
"I was just a bit flat. That's the main thing," Gauff said.
"The level was there at some points, I just didn't sustain it the whole match."
Belgium's Mertens will play former world number one Iga Swiatek in the quarter-finals after the six-time major champion beat American teenager Iva Jovic 6-1 6-3.
Elsewhere, Britain's Arthur Fery beat Marin Cilic 7-6 (7-2) 6-1 in the Shanghai Masters first round.
Fery came back from a break down in the first set before dominating the former US Open champion in the second to claim his first ATP Tour win since August.
The 24-year-old will face Russia's 26th seed Karen Khachanov next.

Eligible Amazon Prime customers do not need to do anything to receive their payment. The FTC is also warning people that some scammers are exploiting the legitimate class action lawsuit to steal people's personal information. The FTC said it will not call any eligible customers, nor will they demand money or promise a special prize.
Rumors are spreading online about supposed payouts from a class action lawsuit benefiting Amazon Prime subscribers.
Social media users on platforms like Reddit and Facebook shared screenshots of notifications about the lawsuit or receiving payment (screenshotted). Some online posters claimed they received payment, whereas others asked if the settlement was real.
Snopes readers also searched the website for information on the Amazon Prime lawsuit.
This is a legitimate settlement involving payouts to eligible Amazon Prime customers.
The Federal Trade Commission reached a $2.5 billion settlement with Amazon over allegations that the company "enrolled tens of millions of customers in Amazon Prime subscriptions without their knowledge or consent" and "made it difficult for customers to cancel their Amazon Prime subscriptions." As part of the settlement, Amazon did not admit fault.
An official notice on the Federal Trade Commission website states that Amazon began sending payments in November 2025 and "will continue to send automatic refunds to eligible Prime customers through April 2027."
Customers who received a previous payment of up to $51 may receive additional payments due to a revised settlement order. Eligible customers may receive up to $200 in total (so up to $149 if you received a $51 payment previously).
It is worth noting, however, that the FTC is also warning people that scammers are calling people and claiming to be part of the Amazon class action lawsuit payouts.
"The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. And no one from Amazon will ever ask you for money to get a refund," the FTC website said. "Only scammers say they can get you special access or a guaranteed refund."
Eligibility and payment process
According to the FTC, eligible claimants do not need to take any actions to receive a refund. Amazon will send automatic refund payments by mailed check, PayPal or Venmo, and all you need to do is accept the payment.
Here's how to know if you're eligible, per the FTC's news release (emphasis theirs):
Who is eligible for a refund?
Under the revised settlement order, you are eligible for a refund if you meet all three requirements:
- You are an Amazon Prime customer in the United States.
- You signed up for an Amazon Prime subscription through a "challenged enrollment flow" or tried to cancel through the online cancellation flow but were unable to do so between June 23, 2019 and June 23, 2025.
- You used no more than 20 Amazon Prime Benefits (including Prime Music or Prime Video products offered for free to Prime subscribers) in any 12-month period following Amazon Prime enrollment.
The "challenged enrollment flows" are universal Prime decision page, shipping selection page, single page checkout, or the Prime Video enrollment flow.
No action is needed to receive a refund. You do not have to file a claim, respond to a notice, or complete any forms. Amazon will send automatic payments to eligible customers.
Customers who have issues receiving payments or questions can reach out to admin@SubscriptionMembershipSettlement.com or call 1-888-999-8094. The official website for notifications about this class action lawsuit is at www.SubscriptionMembershipSettlement.com, per the FTC.
How to check if a class action lawsuit is legitimate
In the case of the Amazon settlement, the FTC's news release on the federal agency's official website — with a ".gov" domain — lends it legitimacy.
However, Snopes has previously verified class action lawsuits that are not brought by the government. In those cases, it's worth checking the lawsuit's case number in PACER, a public database for federal electronic court records, or CourtListener, a more user-friendly nonprofit repository that pulls information from PACER documents and other court records.
Even if the FTC did not make an announcement, for example, the screenshots of payments shared on social media include a case number for the Amazon settlement: 2:23-cv-01372.
Searching that case number in CourtListener returned two pages of results. On the second page, there's a case called "In re: Amazon Return Policy Litigation." That's proof that a real lawsuit has been filed. The case page includes links to all the documents in the court docket for that particular case. A document titled, "Exhibit A - Amazon Settlement Agreement" states that a settlement was reached.

India has been blessed with vast cricketing riches. The latest proof of its ever-widening talent pool is that four teams of international regulars and hopefuls have been playing in four different locations across three formats.
But an eyebrow is always raised when it comes to one particular player profile – the pace-bowling all-rounder. Hardik Pandya is undoubtedly the numero uno, but recurring injuries have kept him out of the national side for a while. Nitish Kumar Reddy is the next in line, but injuries haven’t been kind to him either.
This has opened the door for young Suryansh Shedge from Mumbai to spend time around the first-team setup. The selectors have earmarked him as a future option, and his latest effort with the ball for India A against Australia A proves why.
On a surface that offered little extra bounce for the pacers, the 23-year-old registered his career-best List-A figures of 4/35 in the first one-dayer in Puducherry.
Yash Thakur’s opening burst in the first PowerPlay had given Suryansh an idea of the conditions. The area just short of good length was the one to target.
The first over didn’t quite go to plan, and the pacer conceded 11, including two boundaries. But when he got the ball for a second spell, he found the sweet spot.
“After the first over, I realised that the ball is coming on nicely at full length or conventional good length. So I used the scrambled seam a lot and tried to hit the deck, which gave me a lot of positives,” the all-rounder said. Suryansh has always been a hard-lengths bowler. He says it comes naturally due to his action. “If I can master that length, it will always give me an upper hand against batters,” he says.
ALSO READ | McSweeney, Beardman set up Australia’s big win over India A in first one-day game
But what will excite him and the coaches tracking him will be how he picked up his next three wickets. Australia A skipper Will Sutherland and Nathan McSweeney had warded off the pace threat, and their run accumulation against spin helped swell the partnership to 141.
Suryansh struck again in his third spell, this time reversing the old ball into Sutherland, rattling his stumps. The late movement also accounted for Todd Murphy and Spencer Johnson, both nicking behind slightly fuller balls.
Suryansh came into this shadow tour after a brief injury setback. He played three T20Is in three different countries in June and July, but was forced to spend some time at the BCCI Centre of Excellence. “I took the injury as a blessing in disguise because it was just the start of the season. I got that time off to get more clarity, get fitter and come back as a better cricketer,” he said.
It was here that he spent time with Hardik, whom he eventually replaced in the India A squad. “Master your stock ball. That will be your USP. When someone is attacking you, you can always fall back on that. If that gets mentally set in your mind, you’ll find it easier,” this was the senior all-rounder’s advice to his junior partner, Shedge recollects.
Speaking to Sportstar in the winter of 2024, after his heroics with the bat helped Mumbai to the Syed Mushtaq Ali title, the then 21-year-old revealed he began practising bowling seriously only at 19. He has made rapid strides since, for which he credits the work done behind the scenes and the tips he picked up from speaking with senior players.
“I think when you’re bowling in different situations, you learn a lot about yourself. Especially when you’re around people who have won games for India. That’s what I’ve tried to do in the last year — learn as much as I can,” he said.
“For the last two years, I’ve been in the COE circuit, going there for camps, talking to different coaches and senior players. I learned a lot during the three T20 series. It gave me a lot of clarity as to what my strengths are and what I need to work on,” he explained.
He may have bowled the most important spell of his life so far, but Suryansh was dejected post-match for failing to save India from trouble with the bat. But the middle-order finishing prowess that helped him bag an IPL contract with the Punjab Kings and saved India A from collapse away in Sri Lanka shows there is enough potential to work with.

“I started playing cricket because I love the sport. I want to grow as a player and as a person. So that process is always ongoing. God has been kind because of the hard work I’ve put in, so I’ll continue to do that till the day I’m playing,” he said.
Suryansh’s international career is still very much in its infancy. If he sustains his clarity of thought and ready-for-anything attitude, he very well could be one of the answers to India’s quest for the perfect team balance.

Another day and another new model grabs the limelight. Product teams scramble to see how it can be used for their own operations and systems. But a new model can look great in a demo and still make a product worse. It may cost less but respond too slowly, pass offline tests but fail with real customers, or behave differently once traffic and context change. That is why the engineering question is shifting from which model to use to how teams prove a model change is safe and worth making. At Inc42’s The CTO Summit 2026 last week, leaders from Swiggy, Rapido, Razorpay, ShareChat, Shadowfax and Meesho described building evaluations or evals and monitoring into the model lifecycle. And as platforms and products grow, evals are quickly becoming a key differentiation in the AI strategy. The accounts of these unicorns and massive listed tech companies point to a practical shift in the product and software development lifecycle: model choice is becoming a continuing production decision, and evaluation is the evidence needed to make it. Evals, short for evaluations, are systematic tests used to measure how well an AI model or system performs a specific task. But what should teams measure, and how can they tell whether the measurement itself is reliable? Let’s unravel it in today’s edition of The AI Shift. Why Evals Are Becoming Critical Swiggy’s experience shows the cost of not building for change early. Madhusudhan Rao, CTO at Swiggy, said an early contact-centre agent was tied to one model. When the provider faced capacity constraints, migrating took nearly a month. Swiggy now uses evaluations and experimentation to make model changes easier. “Treat the model as replaceable, invest in the workflow, the evals,” Rao said. The point is not to test models in isolation. A switch has to be assessed against the task and the product: does it improve quality, latency or cost without disrupting the customer experience? Nitin Jain, CTO, ShareChat & Moj, described evaluations as an internal check and A/B testing as a way to observe customer impact. “Eval and A/B testing are just one or like different ways of doing the similar thing,” he said. Shadowfax offers a production example. Vaibhav Khandelwal, cofounder and CTO, Shadowfax, said the company was on its third model iteration for a delivery-partner support bot. Evaluations and observability let the team compare iterations on cost, speed and accuracy. The useful question for an AI team is not whether a model scored higher once, but whether the new version performs better on the product’s actual operating measures. Those measures cannot be chosen from a generic checklist alone. A support bot may fail by repeating itself, going silent or misunderstanding a delivery partner, while a commerce assistant may fail to understand a request. Teams first need to examine real outputs and identify the specific errors that matter to their users. Anand Jain, head of engineering, Meesho, said evaluations give the company confidence when comparing one model with another. The transcript does not specify Meesho’s evaluation metrics or thresholds, but his point highlights a gap CTOs should address: what does “better” mean for each workflow, and what level of regression is acceptable before a model change is rejected? An evaluation system also needs validation. Eternal’s engineering team, in a post about its in-house Gavel evaluation infrastructure, says it compares automated judges with human review. At the time of writing in July 2026, Gavel had already evaluated more than a million items and some of its AI judges were close to human quality checks on roughly 90% of critical flaws. That example illustrates both the potential and the caveat: automated scoring can extend review, but teams still need to check whether the judge catches the failures they care about. Monitoring Has To Meet Action Even a well-designed pre-release evaluation cannot guarantee that a model will keep performing once users and conditions change. Monitoring needs to show what is happening in production, identify a meaningful regression and connect it to a decision: keep the model, adjust it or roll back. Khandelwal’s emphasis on observability and Rao’s account of a slow provider migration show that evaluation and operational readiness are linked. For companies, the loop should run from real user outputs to failure categories, from those failures to targeted tests, and from test results to a release or rollback decision. Cost belongs in that loop too. Shadowfax compares model iterations on cost as well as accuracy and speed; Swiggy’s model portability work is intended to make changing providers less disruptive. Eternal’s Gavel post adds a practical illustration of scale: it says automated review of a voicebot call costs around ₹10, compared with roughly ₹450 for human review. That is a company-reported example, not evidence that human oversight can be removed. The stronger takeaway is that automation can widen coverage while human reviewers define and validate the quality bar. As Indian companies move AI systems into customer-facing and operational workflows, evals will matter most when they change what teams do: block a weak release, surface a failure early, or show that a cheaper model is good enough. The advantage will go to teams that can make model changes quickly without asking users to absorb the risk. Prompt Of The Week What prompts and hacks are CTOs, CEOs and cofounders using these days to streamline their work? Here's Yash Varyani, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) and co-founder of Drizz, with a prompt he uses to review pull requests. "You are a CTO reviewing a pull request. I'll paste the diff. Skip line-by-line review; use five gates. Gate 1: Problem Right reviewers? Meaningful or housekeeping? How do other industries solve it? Product-agnostic version? Two-way or one-way door? Impact on retention, acquisition, expansion? Gate 2: Production Blast radius? Deployment and change risks? Monitoring needed before merge? Metrics affected, and how are they improved? Gate 3: Architecture Before vs after: better, or just more complex? Improved architecture or added surface area? Patterns used or missed (Port Adapter, DDD, CQRS)? Control plane separate from data plane? Two-way door? Better alternatives? Can Customer Success run this without engineering? Gate 4: Code Health Mental model, focus areas, best file review order? Cross-repo consistency? Flag coupling, cohesion, circular dependencies, SOLID violations, broken abstractions, type safety gaps, redundancy, blocking async code. Questions answered for engineering, PM, sales, CS? Old code cleaned up? Matches repo structure and UX conventions? Gate 5: Ship Readiness Works across Android, iOS, watch, car, device sizes? Client CI/CD impact? Multi-tenancy respected? Memory or resource risks? Unit tests enough, or integration needed? Customer reporting impact? More auditable? Central docs updated? More agentic approach? Can a machine learn from the output and improve the process? End with the top risk, the biggest missed opportunity, and a verdict: SHIP, REVISE, or REDESIGN." Son of Zambian bishop detained in post-election raid fears for his father's safety
The son of detained Zambian opposition politician Bishop Trevor Mwamba has told the BBC he is concerned for his father's safety after the former Bishop of Botswana was detained along with 10 other opposition figures by authorities.
Eno Mwamba said his father, who is leader of the United National Independence Party, has been charged with treason following President Hakainde Hichilema's disputed election victory.
The opposition politicians have been held since a raid by security forces on 14 August.
Opposition leader Brian Mundubile, head of the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP), had gone into hiding after disputing the election result, but has since also been detained by the authorities.
The government accuses the opposition of planning an armed insurgency and have charged the detained politicians with treason. They have denied the charges.

2 అక్టోబర్ 2026న, ముంబైలోని శివాజీ పార్క్లో కాక్రోచ్ జనతా పార్టీ (CJP) నిరసన చేపట్టింది. భారత ఎన్నికల సంఘం (ECI) తమకు జవాబుదారీగా ఉండాలని, ప్రధాన ఎన్నికల కమిషనర్ జ్ఞానేశ్ కుమార్ రాజీనామా చేయాలని వారు డిమాండ్ చేశారు. ముంబై పోలీసులు ఈ సమావేశానికి అనుమతి నిరాకరించినప్పటికీ, వేలాది మంది నిరసనలో పాల్గొని నినాదాలు చేశారు. అయితే, సమావేశంపై విధించిన ఆంక్షలను ఉల్లంఘించారనే ఆరోపణలతో 400–500 మంది పాల్గొన్న వారిపై పోలీసులు ఎఫ్ఐఆర్ నమోదు చేశారు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ).
ఈ నేపథ్యంలో, సోషల్ మీడియాలో ఒక వీడియో (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ) ముంబైలోని శివాజీ పార్క్లో జరిగిన CJP నిరసనకు సంబంధించినవిగా షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు. దీని వెనుక ఉన్న వాస్తవాన్ని ఈ కథనంలో పరిశీలిద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: ఈ వీడియో 2 అక్టోబర్ 2026న ముంబైలోని శివాజీ పార్క్లో జరిగిన కాక్రోచ్ జనతా పార్టీ (CJP) నిరసనకు సంబంధించింది.
ఫాక్ట్: ఈ వీడియో 2 అక్టోబర్ 2026న శివాజీ పార్క్లో జరిగిన CJP నిరసనకు సంబంధించింది కాదు. ఈ వీడియోను న్యూఢిల్లీలోని జంతర్ మంతర్ వద్ద CJP నిర్వహించిన నిరసన సమయంలో చిత్రీకరించారు. కాబట్టి, ఈ పోస్టులో చేసిన క్లెయిమ్ తప్పుదారి పట్టిస్తుంది.
వైరల్ వీడియోను పరిశీలించగా, బారికేడ్లపై ‘Delhi Police’ అని రాసి ఉన్నట్లు గుర్తించాము. దీని ద్వారా, ఈ వీడియో ముంబైలో కాకుండా ఢిల్లీలో చిత్రీకరించినవని తెలుస్తోంది.
ఆ తర్వాత, వైరల్ వీడియోలోని కీ ఫ్రేమ్లతో రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ నిర్వహించగా, ‘Indian Sawarn Samaj News’ అనే ఫేస్బుక్ పేజీలో 2026 ఆగస్టు 8న అప్లోడ్ చేసిన అదే వీడియో లభించింది. ఈ వీడియోను ఢిల్లీలో ధర్మేంద్ర ప్రధాన్ రాజీనామా చేయాలని డిమాండ్ చేస్తూ CJP నిర్వహించిన నిరసనగా పేర్కొంటూ క్యాప్షన్తో అప్లోడ్ చేశారు. దీంతో, ఈ వైరల్ వీడియో 2026 అక్టోబర్ 2న ముంబైలోని శివాజీ పార్క్లో జరిగిన CJP నిరసనకు ముందే రికార్డ్ చేసినదని స్పష్టమవుతోంది.
అలాగే, వైరల్ వీడియోలో కనిపిస్తున్న ఎత్తైన భవనాన్ని జియోలొకేట్ చేయగా, అది న్యూఢిల్లీలో ఉన్న జై సింగ్ మార్గ్, జంతర్ మంతర్ ప్రాంతంలో ఉన్నట్లు గుర్తించాము. వైరల్ వీడియోలో కనిపిస్తున్న భవనం, గూగుల్ మ్యాప్స్ స్ట్రీట్ వ్యూలో కనిపిస్తున్న అదే భవనం మధ్య పోలికను కింద చూడవచ్చు.
చివరిగా, ఢిల్లీలోని CJP నిరసన వీడియోను ముంబై నిరసనకు సంబంధించినదిగా తప్పుగా షేర్ చేశారు.

- Fortnite has fueled speculation around an upcoming One Piece crossover by replying to a fan post.
- The image posted by a fan on social media features characters from One Piece, Demon Slayer, and Chainsaw Man in a waiting room.
- Fortnite replied to the post by implying that the characters "take a number" in the form of a ticket to wait their turn for a crossover.
Fortnite players have been waiting for a One Piece collab ever since it appeared on a player survey earlier this year. Since then, leakers and dataminers have fueled such a crossover, but Epic has been mum until now. Fortnite’s official X page replied to a fan post featuring characters from One Piece, Demon Slayer, and Chainsaw Man on October 6, 2026, thus hinting at an upcoming crossover.
Fortnite One Piece Collab Teased as Epic Asks Luffy to “Take a Number” and Wait His Turn
The post mentioned above contained an image that was tweeted by user ThunderOptimism on X on September 29. In the image, characters like Denji, Tenjiro Kamado, and Monkey D. Luffy can be seen standing in a waiting room, which implies they’re “waiting their turn” for a Fortnite collab. The OP posted the picture with the caption, “Got a idea,” and added speech bubbles to the characters inside.
In the image, Asta from Black Clover gets called to Fortnite after someone announces, “Now calling Asta,” while Monkey D. Luffy fumes in the background, stating, “Are you for real?” Fortnite officially replied to this fan post, which featured an image of a “take-a-number” dispenser, with a ticket that has the number “A84.”
The number itself does not correlate with any of the characters present, but it does confirm that Epic has plans for Fortnite collabs with One Piece, Demon Slayer, and Chainsaw Man in the future; possibly once the ongoing Fortnitemares 2026 event is done and dusted.
Two of the characters (Freddy Fazbear and Asta) featured in the fan’s post were added for Fortnitemares 2026, with the Fortnite FNAF collab being the most hyped one yet. The others will have to wait their turn to get called to the Battle Bus. Nonetheless, with Fortnite officially replying, it’s not mere hype and can be taken as the first teaser for what’s to come.
That said, fans have all unanimously agreed that Fortnite’s reply to the fan’s post confirms the One Piece collab. To add some credibility, a One Piece collab with Rocket League has leaked, which means getting one for Fortnite cannot be ruled out. However, until we get more tangible leaks, we can’t say for certain what Epic Games has planned.
But more likely, if a One Piece collab is in the making, expect it to arrive during the Fortnite Mini Season. As per the Fortnite 2026 Roadmap, it’s slated to begin on November 1 and will be the last phase for this storyline before Chapter 8 begins.

Worldwide, traditional medicine is used by billions of people for their health and well-being. At a signing ceremony in Geneva, the Government of India committed US$ 85 million over 10 years, 2022–2032, to support the programming of the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre. India’s 10-year financial contribution will support a cross-sectoral program of work to strengthen the evidence base for traditional medicine by providing data and evidence on traditional medicine policies, practice, products, and public use.
The WHO-India donor agreement is part of a US$ 250 million investment from India in support of the establishment of the WHO Global Centre of Traditional Medicine in 2022, which includes financial support for the workplan of the Centre, interim premises and a new building. This support will scale up WHO’s capacities on traditional medicine across technical divisions and regions in the spirit of global collaboration and solidarity. Part of this substantial contribution from the Government of India will also be included in WHO’s Investment Round to resource WHO’s core work during 2025–2028.
Photo: WHO/Lindsay Mackenzie
“India’s commitment and leadership in expanding the evidence-based contribution of traditional medicine to the health and well-being of all people and the planet, comes at an opportune moment,” said Dr Bruce Aylward, Assistant Director-General of the Universal Health Coverage and Life Course division of WHO. “Traditional medicine, supported within national health systems, can allow us to reach those most often left behind. Integration of traditional practice and knowledge is critical to achieving health for all.”
“The signing of this donor agreement is a major milestone towards achieving the shared vision of Honourable Prime Minister of India Shri Narendra Modi and WHO Director-General Tedros for the development of the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre at Jamnagar in India,” said Vice Minister Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary of the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India.
“India remains committed to supporting WHO in its work to strengthen traditional medicine systems globally for achieving universal health coverage and serving the entire humanity, especially through this Global Centre in Jamnagar, which would help focus these efforts to benefit all Member States,” said Ambassador Arindam Bagchi, Permanent Representative of India to the UN and other International Organizations in Geneva.
The WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre is is a knowledge hub focusing on five inter-connected areas of work: research and evidence; primary health care and universal health coverage; Indigenous Knowledges and biodiversity; digital health applications; and the biennial WHO Global Traditional Medicine Summit and collaborations. The Centre is led by Dr Shyama Kuruvilla, Director a.i.
The first WHO traditional medicine global summit was held in August 2023 in Gujarat, resulting in the a multistakeholder action agenda, the Gujarat Declaration. The next WHO Global Summit is planned for November 2025, following up on the anticipated launch of the 2025–2034 Global Strategy for Traditional Medicine at the 78th World Health Assembly in May 2025.
India’s support for traditional medicine has been expressed through a variety of long-standing partnerships with WHO. In 2023, India signed a five-year agreement to support the technical work of WHO’s Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine (TCI) unit. The unit is supporting the development of the Member State-requested new WHO traditional medicine global strategy (2025 - 2034), and publishes key benchmark documents, standardized terminologies, and other evidence-informed technical products to support the safe and effective integration of traditional medicine in national health systems.  
The Centre and TCI collaborate closely with teams across WHO to advance WHO’s multisectoral agenda on traditional medicine, including through regular meetings of the WHO Technical Expert Network, coordinated by the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre and TCI, to promote a One WHO approach on traditional medicine across headquarters, regional and country office.

India recorded 3,832 new leprosy cases among children in 2025-26, including 37 who had Grade-2 disability (G2D) at diagnosis — an indicator of delayed detection. The child caseload was 91.6% higher than the National Leprosy Eradication Programme's (NLEP) target of 2,000 cases for the year.
The figures, from the latest NLEP annual report for 2025-26, come even as India pursues the National Strategic Plan for Leprosy 2023-27, which seeks to interrupt transmission at the district level by 2027. Under the roadmap, a district is considered to have interrupted transmission after reporting zero new indigenous child cases for five consecutive years.
The NLEP's programme objectives include zero disability among new child cases and a national G2D rate of less than one case per million population. The roadmap projects 1,000 child cases and a G2D rate of 0.5 per million for 2026-27.
The appearance of children among newly detected cases matters beyond the absolute number. The World Health Organisation (WHO) considers new cases among children below 15 years an indicator of recent transmission, while G2D among newly detected patients indicates delayed diagnosis.
The WHO also says disabilities among newly detected child cases signal both delayed detection and ongoing transmission.
India recorded 63 children with G2D in 2019-20, followed by 35 in 2020-21, 41 in 2021-22, 55 in 2022-23 and 45 in 2023-24. The continued detection of children with G2D contrasts with the NLEP's objective of zero disability among new child cases.
The latest numbers therefore raise a fundamental epidemiological question: if India is working to interrupt transmission by 2027, why are children still developing leprosy, and why are some reaching diagnosis only after visible disability has appeared?
India detected 91,783 new leprosy cases in 2025-26, according to the Union Health Ministry. The prevalence rate was 0.56 per 10,000 population, and 1,945 patients had Grade-2 disability at diagnosis, accounting for 2.12% of all newly detected cases. The national G2D rate was 1.34 per million, above the NLEP's target of less than one case per million.
According to the WHO's latest global update, India reported the world's largest number of newly detected leprosy cases in 2025, with 91,783 cases, followed by Brazil with 22,901 and Indonesia with 16,292. Together, the three countries accounted for 78.3% of all new cases reported globally. The WHO notes that, although the update is for 2025, India reported data for April 2025 to March 2026.
India also reported the world's largest number of new child leprosy cases in the WHO's 2025 global update, with 3,832 cases.
The WHO figures and the NLEP figures refer to the same reporting period for India — April 2025 to March 2026 — although the WHO presents India's data in its 2025 global table. The WHO table records 3,832 child cases and 37 child cases with G2D for India.
Dr. Kabir Sardana, Professor and Head of Dermatology at ABVIMS-Dr. RML Hospital, Delhi, attributed the continuing burden partly to gaps in case detection.
"Data points to the fact that there is poor detection, which is why we are seeing more children with leprosy," he said.
The Health Ministry identifies high-endemic and hard-to-reach areas as priorities for intensified case detection. The NLEP emphasises active case detection, household contact surveys and focused campaigns, along with special plans for hard-to-reach areas. The programme also identifies stigma and discrimination as continuing concerns.
The WHO says prolonged, close contact with untreated cases allows transmission to continue, while the disease's long incubation period makes interruption difficult. New child cases are considered an indicator of recent transmission, although the presence of a child case cannot by itself establish when or where the infection occurred. The WHO notes that symptoms can appear years after infection.
Leprosy, or Hansen's disease, is a chronic bacterial infection caused mainly by Mycobacterium leprae. It primarily affects the skin and peripheral nerves. Transmission occurs mainly through prolonged, close contact with an untreated person. The disease is curable with multidrug therapy, a combination of antibiotics provided free through public-health programmes.
Children and household contacts are particularly important to surveillance because a new child case can indicate ongoing transmission within a community. However, the presence of a child case cannot by itself establish when or where the infection occurred. The average incubation period is about five years and can be considerably longer.
India's child caseload has fallen substantially from a decade ago, but the decline has not been linear. The country detected 11,365 children with leprosy in 2014-15, 11,389 in 2015-16 and 11,770 in 2016-17. The number fell to 10,287 in 2017-18, 9,227 in 2018-19 and 7,859 in 2019-20.
Child detections fell sharply during the COVID-19 period, reaching 3,753 in 2020-21, before rising to 4,107 in 2021-22. They fell again to 2,363 in 2022-23 and 2,335 in 2023-24, before rising to 3,832 in 2025-26. Changes in reported case numbers also reflect the intensity and reach of case detection, making it difficult to interpret the trend as a direct measure of transmission alone.
The Health Ministry has identified high-priority States and districts where the burden remains concentrated. Twenty-three districts in Chhattisgarh, 21 in Jharkhand, 18 each in Maharashtra and Odisha, and 10 in Madhya Pradesh had a prevalence rate above one case per 10,000 population, according to the Ministry.
These figures identify districts with prevalence above the elimination threshold; they should not be read as meaning that these are the only States or districts with continuing transmission.
For a disease that is curable, and for which early detection and treatment can prevent the progression to disability, the continued detection of children — including some already showing Grade-2 disability — highlights the tension between programme targets and what is still being detected in communities.

A surprise suspected accomplice has been arrested in connection with a mass school shooting in Canada that was made notorious after an 18-year-old allegedly killed six children after discussing it with the AI chatbot ChatGPT.
The US Department of Justice said Tuesday it had detained James Codey Bryant, 30, a resident of western Washington state, on a charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country.
Bryant offered money and “technical advice” to the suspected shooter for six months leading up to the killings, the justice department alleged.
Canadian police have identified the suspect in this year’s massacre of eight people – including her mother and half-brother, as well as the six children, making it the second-deadliest school shooting in the country’s history – as Jesse Van Rootselaar, who has a history of mental health problems.
It had been known that Van Rootselaar had used ChatGPT to plan the attack, which took place in February. The safety team at OpenAI, the company that owns the chatbot, flagged Van Rootselaar internally after she conducted conversations with it about gun violence, but the company did not alert police. It did reportedly close Van Rootselaar’s account, but she started a second one that was not closed. Victims’ families and the province of British Columbia have sued OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, for failing to report her behaviour.
It was not previously known publicly that Van Rootselaar was also talking to a human about her plans.
In a joint press conference with the justice department and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) on Tuesday, authorities alleged that Bryant and Van Rootselaar met on the now-defunct messaging service Omegle about three years prior to the shooting and kept in contact.
Neil Floyd, acting US attorney, and W Mike Herrington, the special agent in charge for the FBI’s Seattle bureau, said they believe Bryant sent Van Rootselaar about $100 to buy new shoes and aabout $15 for a lighter.
Authorities said there is no indication so far that the two suspects ever met in person.
According to an indictment obtained by CBC, Bryant was “knowingly and wilfully” conspiring with Van Rootselaar beginning in or before August 2025.
That August, Bryant told Van Rootselaar the pair should “find a way to delete” their messages, and in mid-December Bryant suggested getting a VPN to avoid detection for “posting a shooting video online”, according to the court document reviewed by CBC.
Police said that on several occasions Bryant tried to talk Van Rootselaar out of committing the attack, but did not contact law enforcement.
They added that after Van Rootselaar shot and killed her mother and brother in their family home, she was unable to start the car. Bryant advised her on how to turn on the engine, thereby allowing the shooter to reach the school and execute the attack, authorities said.
Bryant also allegedly agreed to livestream the mass shooting, which Harrington said police were not sure Van Rootselaar would have committed had Bryant not done so.
It was not clear whether the suspect was represented by a lawyer. Bryant will be prosecuted in the US as a US citizen under an investigation by the FBI, which said it will continue working closely with Canadian authorities.

Ryder Cup 2027: Sergio Garcia targets European team spot and refuses to rule out PGA Tour return
Sergio Garcia is targeting a return to the European Ryder Cup team for the 2027 tournament at Adare Manor, with the Spaniard also refusing to rule out a return to the PGA Tour watch the Open de Espana live on Sky Sports Golf from Thursday at 1pm
Wednesday 7 October 2026 18:18, UK
Sergio Garcia is desperate to be involved in next year's Ryder Cup, either as a player or vice-captain, with his time on LIV Golf appearing to be coming to an end.
The Saudi-backed breakaway league filed for bankruptcy last month, with its restructuring plan likely to release players from their existing contracts ahead of a potential LIV 2.0 relaunch.
This week, Garcia successfully secured a court ruling to lift an automatic stay on his contract, allowing him to seriously consider his options for 2027.
Europe's all-time leading Ryder Cup points scorer now has his sights firmly set on Adare Manor next September.
"I think everything is an option," he told a press conference at the Open de Espana in Madrid.
"That doesn't mean I won't go or that I'll definitely stay with LIV, but settling the LIV 1.0 matter now avoids potential repercussions related to that contract.
"I don't really know how things will end up with the DP World Tour regarding LIV 2.0, we'll have to see, [but] I want to try and give myself the best chance of making that team.
"Everyone knows how much I love the Ryder Cup and the possibility of playing in another one, or if not, finding some way to help in another way, as vice-captain or something like that could be something very interesting."
Garcia, who has spoken to European captain Luke Donald, added: "I told him that I'm going to do everything possible to see if I can get into that team and I also told him that if I don't get into that team, I'll help in any way I can."
The 2017 Masters champion would first need to regain his DP World Tour membership.
Garcia resigned his membership in 2023 after being sanctioned for playing in conflicting LIV events. He later paid around £750,000 in fines in an unsuccessful bid to qualify for the Ryder Cup at Bethpage last year, but ultimately lost his card after failing to meet the minimum number of events.
Garcia has also not ruled out a return to the PGA Tour, although under its rules he would have to serve a suspension until August.
"It's definitely a possibility. I turn 47 in January, and the Champions Tour is a possibility," he said.
"Besides, I'd like the chance to play some of those tournaments, especially the big ones on the Champions Tour. These are things that I'm starting to consider at my age."
